latestRelease.notes:
# Hermes Agent v0.20.2 (v2026.8.16)

**Release Date:** August 16, 2026

> Patch release. This tag rolls up the ~397 PRs merged since v0.20.1 into a stable tagged release for downstream consumers (Docker images, hosted deployments, fresh installs).

---

## About this release

Since v0.20.1 (v2026.8.13, tagged August 13), this window landed **~967 commits** across **~1,279 files** (+128,522 / −7,622) — **~397 merged PRs** of fixes and improvements spanning the desktop app (multi-gateway Connections registry, profile-scoped refreshes, MCP health checks and deep links), the CLI (Windows update probes, Kitty keyboard protocol, chat `-c` hardening), the gateway (persisted model routes, /loop completion, Telegram DM topics), prompt caching for LiteLLM Claude on the OpenAI wire, cron hardening, auth resolution through profile scopes, and installer robustness on both Linux and Windows.

**Full curated release notes for this window will ship with v0.21.0**, which will document everything from v0.20.0 onward — highlights, feature areas, and complete contributor credits. Nothing in this window is skipped.

## Updating

- `hermes update` from an existing install
- Fresh install: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/main/scripts/install.sh | bash`

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/compare/v2026.8.13...v2026.8.16

signals.title: kanban workers (`chat -q`) bypass the rate-limit/failure exit-code mapping → transient provider outage trips the circuit breaker
signals.text: ## Summary A dispatched kanban worker whose agent run dies on a **transient provider failure** (connection drop / timeout / 5xx, after retry exhaustion) exits the process with code **0** and is reaped as a `protocol_violation`, which trips the circuit breaker (`failure_limit`) and permanently blocks the card. The worker did nothing wrong — the provider was briefly unreachable — but the card is left `blocked` and requires a manual `hermes kanban unblock`. Observed on **v0.16.0**. ## Root cause 1. The kanban exit-code mapping — failed run → exit 1, and `rate_limit`/`billing` → `KANBAN_RATE_LIMIT_EXIT_CODE` (75, "requeue without counting a failure") — exists **only in the fully-quiet (`-Q` / `--quiet`) branch** of `main()` in `cli.py`: ```python _exit_code = 0 if isinstance(result, dict) and result.get("failed"): _exit_code = 1 if os.environ.get("HERMES_KANBAN_TASK") and result.get("failure_reason") in ("rate_limit", "billing"): from hermes_cli.kanban_db import KANBAN_RATE_LIMIT_EXIT_CODE as _RL_CODE _exit_code = _RL_CODE sys.exit(_exit_code) ``` 2. But the dispatcher spawns workers via the **single-query (`-q` / `--query`)** path, not quiet mode — `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py` `_default_spawn`: ```python cmd.extend(["chat", "-q", prompt]) # -q == --query, NOT -Q/--quiet ``` `-q`/`--query` and `-Q`/`--quiet` are distinct flags (`hermes_cli/_parser.py`). The single-query branch in `cli.py` runs `cli.chat(query, ...)` then returns with **no exit-code handling at all** — so the process exits 0 regardless of whether `run_conversation` returned `{"failed": True, ...}` (which it does on retry-exhaustion, in `agent/conversation_loop.py`). 3. The dispatcher's reap classifier (`detect_crashed_workers` in `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`) sees a clean rc=0 exit while the task is still `running` and records a `protocol_violation`, tripping the breaker on the first occurrence. Net: a worker that hit a provider blip exits 0, looks like "agent answered conversationally without calling kanban_complete/kanban_block," and the card is force-blocked. ### Real-world trace `feature-adversarial-reviewer` worker; provider briefly unreachable: ``` ⚠️ API call failed (attempt 3/3): APIConnectionError ... Broken pipe ❌ API failed after 3 retries — Connection error. ... process exits 0 ... protocol_violation {exit_code: 0} → gave_up {failures: 2} (failure_limit=2) ``` `APIConnectionError` classifies as `FailoverReason.timeout` (`agent/error_classifier.py`), so even the existing `("rate_limit", "billing")` allowlist would not have spared it. ## Proposed fix **A. Make the kanban exit-code mapping fire on the path workers actually use.** Factor the exit-code decision into a shared helper and call it from BOTH the quiet (`-Q`) branch and the single-query (`-q`) branch. The single-query branch needs access to the run result; `cli.chat()` currently returns only the response string, so either stash the last result on the CLI object (`self._last_run_result = result` right after `run_conversation` returns inside `chat()`) and read it after `cli.chat()`, or have `chat()` return the result dict. ```python def _kanban_worker_exit_code(result) -> int: if not (isinstance(result, dict) and result.get("failed")): return 0 if os.environ.get("HERMES_KANBAN_TASK") and result.get("failure_reason") in _TRANSIENT_PROVIDER_REASONS: from hermes_cli.kanban_db import KANBAN_RATE_LIMIT_EXIT_CODE return KANBAN_RATE_LIMIT_EXIT_CODE return 1 ``` **B. Broaden the no-penalty reason set to all transient provider failures**, not just quota walls — a connection/timeout/5xx outage is no more the task's fault than a 429: ```python _TRANSIENT_PROVIDER_REASONS = frozenset({ "rate_limit", "billing", # existing (quota wall) "timeout", "overloaded", "server_error", # transient provider unavailability }) ``` With both, a transient provider outage on a `-q` worker exits 75 → the dispatcher requeues the card and defers respawn (via `check_respawn_guard`) until the window clears, WITHOUT counting a failure. A genuine task failure still exits 1 → `crashed` (counts toward the breaker), and a real protocol violation (clean exit, task still `running`, no failure flagged) still trips as today. ## Test `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_blocked_sticky.py` and `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_core_functionality.py::test_detect_crashed_workers_protocol_violation_auto_blocks` cover the reap side. Add a case: a `-q` worker whose run returns `{"failed": True, "failure_reason": "timeout"}` exits 75 (not 0) and the card is requeued to `ready` without incrementing `consecutive_failures`. ## Workaround `hermes kanban unblock <task>` resets `consecutive_failures` and re-queues the card.

signals.title: [Bug]: Tool calls in same response overwrite preceding assistant text in Desktop app
signals.text: ### Bug Description Description: In the desktop app, when the assistant generates a substantive text response and then calls a tool (e.g. honcho_conclude) in the same turn, the Desktop app replaces the full response with only the short text after the tool call completes. The first part of the response — which was fully rendered and visible during streaming — disappears. Evidence: User observed the full response appear, then vanish after tool execution. A screenshot shows a faded/greyed-out intermediate text block ("Good, I've saved the new AP info to Honcho.") visible briefly before being replaced by the shorter final response. This suggests the app is rendering intermediate generation states but then only keeping the last assistant text block. Impact: Substantive responses are lost whenever tools are called inline. Users see only the short post-tool confirmation, missing the actual content. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Ask the assistant a question that results in a detailed response 2. Have the assistant call any tool (e.g. honcho_conclude) within the same response 3. Observe the Desktop UI ### Expected Behavior All assistant text blocks in the response are preserved. The full response remains visible after the tool call completes. ### Actual Behavior 1. Full response streams in and is visible 2. Tool call executes 3. Full response is replaced by only the final text block (the short confirmation after the tool) ### Affected Component Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory), Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.), Desktop ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) N/A (CLI only), Desktop ### Debug Report ```shell Report https://paste.rs/Mng9Q agent.log https://paste.rs/cdfac gateway.log https://paste.rs/2aL3l ``` ### Operating System Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Noble Numbat), kernel 6.17.0-35-generic ### Python Version 3.11.15 ### Hermes Version v0.17.0 (2026.6.19), upstream fd2a35b1 ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) The Desktop app likely treats a response as a single mutable text buffer. When streaming includes [text_block_1] → [tool_call] → [text_block_2], the app's state manager replaces the entire buffer with only text_block_2 when the tool call completes, instead of accumulating all text blocks. Likely culprit: The response renderer probably has something like setMessage(response.text) which only holds the latest text block, not an array of blocks. When the tool call triggers a state update, it overwrites with just the post-tool text. ### Proposed Fix (optional) 1. Accumulate, don't replace — the renderer should maintain an array of text blocks and append each new block to the existing response, not replace the whole thing 2. Treat tool calls as inline, not boundaries — the tool call result shouldn't trigger a "response complete" event that flushes prior text 3. Alternatively, separate tool results visually — if the intent is to collapse tool calls, at least preserve the preceding user-visible text ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

signals.title: fix: suppress benign asyncio subprocess-transport teardown noise (RuntimeError: Event loop is closed)
signals.text: ## Summary Benign asyncio teardown noise appears in the chat/TUI when an MCP stdio server's subprocess transport is garbage-collected after the event loop closes. The work completes fine, but this traceback pollutes the display: ``` Exception ignored in: <function BaseSubprocessTransport.__del__ at 0x...> Traceback (most recent call last): .../asyncio/base_subprocess.py, line 126, in __del__ -> self.close() .../asyncio/unix_events.py, line 566, in close -> ... RuntimeError: Event loop is closed ``` ## Reproduction 1. Configure any MCP stdio server whose subprocess transport is GC'd at shutdown 2. Call a tool, then exit the session / let the gateway shut down 3. The traceback prints during interpreter teardown Seen with goshawk (Go) + bladebro (Rust) MCP servers during this session. ## Root cause Classic asyncio race: `BaseSubprocessTransport.__del__` runs during GC after the loop is closed, so `self._check_closed()` raises `RuntimeError('Event loop is closed')`. Cosmetic — the transport already completed — but noisy in the TUI. ## Fix (proposed, locally verified) Override `sys.unraisablehook` to swallow ONLY the benign asyncio-transport teardown (asyncio frames + RuntimeError/ValueError/ResourceWarning), forwarding everything else to the original hook. Same fix hound-mcp ships (dondai44423/master-fetch `server.py` `_quiet_asyncio_del_hook`). Local patch in `tools/mcp_tool.py` verified: import OK, hook active, original preserved. ## Suggested location `tools/mcp_tool.py` at module load (covers all MCP client usage), or globally at the main entry point.

signals.title: [Bug]: Desktop cron uses local profile alias on mapped SSH backend
signals.text: ## Bug description Hermes Desktop can map a local profile label to a differently named profile on a managed SSH gateway. For example: - local Desktop profile: `mara` - connection: managed SSH remote - remote Hermes profile: `default` Opening the full Cron window while `mara` is active fails because Desktop routes the REST request to `mara`'s remote backend but leaves the endpoint filter in the local namespace: ```text /api/cron/jobs?profile=mara ``` The remote backend is scoped to `default`, so it cannot resolve `mara`. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Keep the local `default` profile connected to the local gateway. 2. Configure a second Desktop profile named `mara` to use a managed SSH gateway. 3. Set that SSH connection's remote profile to `default`. 4. Activate `mara` and open the full Cron modal. ## Actual behavior The cron request filters by the Desktop alias `mara`, and the remote backend reports that the profile cannot be found. ## Expected behavior Desktop should keep using `mara` to select the connection, but translate endpoint-level self-profile filters to the configured remote profile: ```text /api/cron/jobs?profile=mara → /api/cron/jobs?profile=default ``` Cross-profile selectors such as `profile=all` or another concrete profile must remain unchanged. ## Root cause `request.profile` correctly selects the per-profile SSH backend in Electron, while the request path independently carries `?profile=<desktop alias>`. The generic REST path resolver knows whether a backend is shared, but it does not know the managed SSH connection's `remoteProfile` mapping. ## Scope The fix should apply at the Electron REST routing boundary so all endpoint-level self-profile filters use the backend namespace, including Cron list and Cron blueprint instantiation, without changing cross-profile selectors. ## Environment - Surface: Hermes Desktop - Connection: per-profile managed SSH - Local profile and remote profile have different names
signals.author: thejpanganiban

signals.title: hermes chat -q (single-query) sessions never finalize — ended_at stays NULL, unbounded session leak
signals.text: ## Summary `hermes chat -q` / `hermes chat --query` (non-interactive single-query mode) creates a session row but never stamps `ended_at` / `end_reason` on exit. Because `hermes sessions prune` only deletes rows where `ended_at IS NOT NULL`, these sessions are invisible to pruning and accumulate without bound. ## Regression (second occurrence) - Originally fixed in v0.18.0 (`_finalize_single_query` in `cli.py` → `agent.close()`). - Regressed again in the v0.20.x one-shot refactor, which moved single-query execution into `hermes_cli/oneshot.py` without carrying the `end_session()` finalization. ## Reproduction ```bash hermes chat -q "Reply with exactly the single word: ok" \ --quiet --model deepseek-v4-flash --provider deepseek ``` Then inspect the resulting session: ```sql SELECT id, source, model, started_at, ended_at, end_reason FROM sessions WHERE id = '<session_id>'; -- ended_at: NULL, end_reason: NULL ``` Expected: `ended_at` stamped with an `end_reason` such as `agent_close` (as the interactive CLI path does). Actual: both `NULL`. Reproduced on v0.20.1 (2026.8.13), install method git, Python 3.11.15. ## Root cause The single-query execution path is `hermes_cli/oneshot.py`. Its `finally` block (lines ~468–492) calls `agent.close()` and `session_db.close()`, but never calls `session_db.end_session()`. The comment at line ~485 states: > agent.close() calls session_db.end_session() but leaves the connection open; close it here to checkpoint the WAL before os._exit skips finalizers. …but that assertion no longer holds: - `agent/agent_init.py:1660` sets `agent._end_session_on_close = True`, yet that flag is never read anywhere in the codebase (only two assignments total; the other is `agent/background_review.py:896` setting it `False`). So `AIAgent.close()` has nothing honoring the flag. - `hermes_cli/oneshot.py` contains zero `session_db.end_session()` calls (verified by grep). For contrast, the interactive CLI path still finalizes correctly via the legacy `cli.py` god-file: `cli.py:18529` calls `self._session_db.end_session(self.agent.session_id, "cli_close")`. ## Why the regression was invisible The existing tests (`tests/cli/test_single_query_session_finalize.py`, `tests/cli/test_chat_q_exit_clear.py`) exercise `cli._finalize_single_query` — the old `cli.py` helper — not the new `hermes_cli/oneshot.py` execution path. There is no end-to-end test asserting that a real `hermes chat -q` run stamps `ended_at`. ## Impact - Every `hermes chat -q` invocation leaks one unfinalized session row. - This is the primary mode used by scripted/automated workers (e.g. our colony dispatcher spawns `hermes chat -q --quiet` on a loop), so the leak is continuous: ~6–8 rows/day in our deployment, ~580 accumulated, 542 MB `state.db`. - `hermes sessions prune` and `auto_prune` (`retention_days`) cannot reclaim these rows because they gate on `ended_at IS NOT NULL`. ## Suggested fix In `hermes_cli/oneshot.py`, finalize the session in the `finally` block — e.g. call `session_db.end_session(agent.session_id, "agent_close")` (mirroring `run_agent.py:4425`) before `session_db.close()`. Add an end-to-end test that runs a real `hermes chat -q` and asserts the resulting session row has `ended_at IS NOT NULL`, so this class of regression cannot recur silently.
signals.author: asperger514

signals.title: hermes update deletes the packaged Desktop app and exits 0 when the desktop rebuild fails
signals.text: # `hermes update` deletes the packaged Desktop app and exits 0 when the desktop rebuild fails ## Summary On Windows, `hermes update` can leave the machine with **no `Hermes.exe` at all** while reporting a successful update. The desktop app is deleted by the rebuild's own `clean` step, the rebuild then fails because the dependencies it needs were never installed, and the failure is not surfaced anywhere — the updater writes `retry exit code: 0` and removes the update marker. The result is an unlaunchable app. It happened twice on the same machine on the same day. ## Environment - OS: Windows 10 Home 19045 (x64) - Hermes Desktop: 40.10.2 (`apps/desktop` package version 0.17.0) - Repo: `main` @ `31e571acf66dbf099b8ed3b2cd42a4f46c7fe372` - Python: 3.11.15 (managed venv) - Bundled Node: v22.23.2 / npm 12.0.2 (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\node`) - Install: managed (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`) ## What happens After the update completes "successfully": ``` apps/desktop/release -> missing apps/desktop/dist -> missing apps/desktop/node_modules -> missing apps/desktop/package.json -> present ``` Desktop shortcut points at `apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked/Hermes.exe`, which no longer exists, so the app simply does not start. `logs/desktop-update-handoff.log` ends with: ``` ✓ Web UI built ✓ Already up to date! npm notice run hermes-agent@1.0.0 postinstall retry exit code: 0 removed update marker (owned) ``` There is **no desktop build section in the log at all** — neither success nor failure. `logs/update.log` does not exist. ## Mechanism 1. The updater runs an `npm install` that does **not** include the desktop workspace's dependencies. From the update log: ``` added 521 packages in 16s ``` Running the documented full install by hand on the same checkout gives: ``` added 769 packages, and audited 1298 packages in 22s ``` A 248-package difference. After the updater's install, the root `node_modules` is missing both `electron` and `katex`, which `apps/desktop` needs to build. (npm's workspace handling also removes `apps/desktop/node_modules` at this point.) 2. The desktop rebuild gate in `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py:4541` still passes, because `release/` has not been touched yet: ```python has_desktop_app = _desktop_packaged_executable(desktop_dir) is not None \ or _desktop_dist_exists(desktop_dir) if (desktop_dir / "package.json").exists() and _resolve_node_runtime_npm() and has_desktop_app: ``` 3. The spawned `hermes desktop --build-only` runs `apps/desktop`'s `prebuild`, which is `npm run clean` — **this deletes `dist/` and `release/`, i.e. the working app**. 4. The build then fails (missing `katex` / `electron`). Reproducing the same build by hand yields: ``` [plugin @tailwindcss/vite:generate:build] apps/desktop/src/styles.css Error: Can't resolve 'katex/dist/katex.min.css' in 'apps/desktop/src' ``` 5. The subprocess failure is not propagated or logged. The updater reports success. ## Why it repeats Once `release/` is gone, `has_desktop_app` is `False`, so every subsequent `hermes update` **silently skips the desktop step forever** — the app can never come back on its own. And after a manual repair (which recreates `release/`), the very next update destroys it again, because step 1–5 replay identically. Both failure modes were observed on this machine. ## Expected behaviour - If a packaged app existed before the update, it must exist after the update, or the updater must report failure loudly (non-zero exit, message in the handoff log, and a visible error in Desktop's update UI). - The rebuild must not delete the current working app until it has everything it needs to produce a replacement. ## Suggested fixes 1. **Don't clean until the build can succeed.** Run `assert-root-install` (and any other preflight) *before* `prebuild`/`clean`, or build to a staging directory and swap on success. A failed build should leave the previous app untouched. 2. **Install the desktop workspace's dependencies** in the updater's `npm install` whenever the desktop rebuild is going to run. The current install is a subset that cannot build the app. 3. **Surface the subprocess result.** Capture `hermes desktop --build-only` stdout/stderr into the handoff log and fail the update when it exits non-zero. 4. **Post-update verification.** After a desktop rebuild, assert the packaged executable exists; if it does not, report failure rather than removing the update marker. 5. Consider making `has_desktop_app` sticky (e.g. a flag written when the user first runs `hermes desktop`) so a missing build directory doesn't permanently disable the rebuild path. ## Workaround With the **bundled** Node on PATH (the PATH Node on this machine is v22.13.1, which fails the repo's `engine-strict` requirement of `>=22.22.0` and npm `<11.10.0 || >=11.17.0`): ```bash export PATH="$LOCALAPPDATA/hermes/node:$PATH" cd "$LOCALAPPDATA/hermes/hermes-agent" npm install cd apps/desktop && npm run pack ``` This restores `release/win-unpacked/Hermes.exe`. It has to be repeated after every update.
signals.author: ameniki

signals.title: [Bug]: Desktop right sidebar snaps to ~2/3 width when dragging the resize seam
signals.text: ### Bug Description In the Desktop app, adjusting the right sidebar (files/review rail) by dragging the seam between the chat area and the rail makes the rail suddenly snap towards the right mid-drag — at roughly 2/3 to 1/2 of its previous size — and it lands at yet another width on release. The rail width does not track the pointer. Two screenshots from the report: the rail before the drag (~433px) and after the snap (~267px). ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Launch Hermes Desktop with the default layout. 2. Open the right rail — Files (`⌘J`) and Review (`⌘G`). 3. Hover the vertical seam between the chat area and the right rail. 4. Click and drag left to widen the rail. 5. The rail snaps to ~2/3 of its size the moment the drag starts, then jumps to a different width on release. ### Expected Behavior The rail width follows the pointer during the drag and lands where the user releases it, stopping at the panes' min/max width clamps (as it does when dragging the seam between Review and Files). ### Actual Behavior The section collapses mid-drag to the inner review zone's clamped size, then pops to a third width on release. Deterministic e2e reproduction on current `main` (default tree, 1220×800, review + files open, drag the workspace|rail seam 120px left): - before: 474px (review 237 + files 237) - mid-drag: **320px — 68% of the size — the "snap"** - after release: 557px (review clamped at max 320 + files 237) - expected: ~594px (follow the pointer) ### Affected Component - Other (Desktop app) ### Messaging Platform - N/A (CLI only) ### Debug Report - Report: https://paste.rs/llEHx - agent.log: https://paste.rs/uVuwQ - gateway.log: https://paste.rs/8ykx4 (Pastes auto-delete after 6 hours.) ### Operating System macOS 26.5.2 ### Python Version 3.11.15 ### Hermes Version Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (2026.8.13) · upstream 165c889e — reproduced on `main` at `165c889e5b` ### Additional Logs / Traceback Reproduction test: `apps/desktop/e2e/sash-snap-repro.spec.ts` (added with the fix PR). It fails on `main` with |preview − commit| = 237px and passes with the fix. ### Root Cause Analysis `startSash` in `apps/desktop/src/components/pane-shell/tree/renderer/tree-split.tsx` resolves each seam side's resize target through `edgeFixedZone` (`track-model.ts`). For a seam side that is a NESTED split — the default tree's right rail is `spl-right` = `COLUMN[ROW[review|files] | terminal]` — the resize target is the INNER edge zone (`grp-review`, 237px), not the section wrapper (474px). The drag preview then applied the inner zone's size as the flex-basis of the whole section wrapper, so mid-drag the section collapsed to the zone's clamped size (320px). The release commit writes the review override (320px), landing the section at review-max + files = 557px — a third width, different from both the pointer and the preview. For a direct group seam (e.g. Review|Files) `zoneEl.parentElement` IS the seam-partner wrapper, so the numbers agree and the drag works — only nested-section seams snap. **When it shipped:** the nested-section sash logic (including this sizing) arrived with the layout-tree renderer ([`63a9bde77b`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/63a9bde77b) and [`0f922002eb`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/0f922002eb), 2026-07-13). The 60fps inline-preview rewrite ([`2c867b05ce`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/2c867b05ce), 2026-07-27) is what makes it *look* like a sudden mid-drag snap (before that it jumped on commit instead). The symptom appears only when the inner zone sits near its clamp — e.g. after the user has already resized Review close to its 320px max. For context: the earlier analysis on #79183 concluded the horizontal sash math was sound on current main; that analysis simulated the old fixed preview rail and the new flex preview zone, but not a fixed zone nested inside a section — the case described here. ### Proposed Fix A fix PR is in progress: the drag preview will write both the seam-partner wrapper (sized from its rendered width at pointerdown) and the resize target's flex item (the inner zone), mirroring exactly what the release commit writes. Clamp and commit math unchanged. The PR carries the deterministic regression test (`apps/desktop/e2e/sash-snap-repro.spec.ts`). - [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR
signals.author: DavidMetcalfe

signals.title: [Bug]: Desktop Review pane "Create PR" always reports generic "is gh installed and authenticated?" even when gh is fine
signals.text: # Issue Draft: Desktop Review-pane "Create PR" button always reports `gh pr create failed (is gh installed and authenticated?)` — even when gh is installed, authenticated, and `gh auth status` is green **Status**: DRAFT — awaiting your review before `gh issue create`. Do NOT auto-post. **Target repo**: `NousResearch/hermes-agent` **Created by**: mugualucheshen (already authenticated via `gh auth status`) **Date**: 2026-08-16 **Local Hermes**: v0.20.1 (2026.8.13), upstream 7095e23e, local 5d526de2 (+1 carried commit) **Affected version**: Desktop `apps/desktop` v0.17.0, commit `56526bc0d3` ("Merge pull request #87630 from kshitijk4poor/fix/kitty-extended-keys-proper") — this is the commit that introduced the affected file. **Affected component**: Desktop (Electron app) → Review pane → ship-bar → PR button **Affected file**: `apps/desktop/electron/git-review-ops.ts`, function `reviewCreatePr()` at lines 765-779, and the helper `runGh()` at lines 35-44. --- ## Bug Description Clicking the PR icon button on the right-side audit panel of the Hermes Desktop app ("创建 PR" / "Create PR") fails with a misleading toast: > gh pr create failed (is gh installed and authenticated?) But `gh` IS installed and authenticated on the same machine. `gh auth status` reports a clean login with full `repo` scope. The toast is a generic fallback that hides the real failure. This is reproducible on macOS in any repo where the branch state doesn't satisfy `gh pr create --fill`'s expectations — e.g. when the upstream tracking branch is missing, when there's no commit ahead, when push hasn't completed yet, or when the local git binary resolution fails. Any non-zero exit from `gh pr create` triggers the same wrong message. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. `hermes update` to v0.20.1 (current `main`). 2. Launch the Hermes Desktop app. 3. Open any git repo (right sidebar → Review pane). 4. Make a commit ahead of the default branch on a local branch that does **not** yet have an upstream tracking ref set on the remote (e.g. a freshly cut branch). 5. Click the small PR-icon button on the right edge of the commit/ship bar. 6. Observe the toast: `gh pr create failed (is gh installed and authenticated?)`. 7. In the same shell, verify: `gh auth status` → green, `gh --version` → 2.86.0, `which gh` → `/opt/homebrew/bin/gh`. The error is a lie. A second reproducer: in a repo where the working branch is in a state that would normally cause `gh pr create` to print a useful stderr like `no commits between main and feature`, the toast is identical and the user is never told the real reason. ## Expected Behavior The error toast should surface `gh`'s real stderr so the user can act on it — for example: - `no commits between main and feature` - `aborted: you must first push the current branch` - `failed to run git: git: command not found` - `Your push would publish a private email address` If the failure is genuinely "gh not installed / not authenticated", the message should still be that — but only when that's actually what gh reported, not as a generic fallback for every error. A useful UX would mirror what the gh CLI itself does: show `gh`'s raw stderr tail in the toast, prefixed by which step failed (push vs create-vs-create). ## Actual Behavior A single fixed toast string regardless of root cause: > gh pr create failed (is gh installed and authenticated?) The user can't tell from the UI whether `gh` is missing, whether auth is broken, whether push failed, whether the branch has no commits, or whether the local git binary couldn't be resolved. They have to open a terminal and run `gh pr create` by hand to find out. ## Root Cause Analysis The bug lives in `apps/desktop/electron/git-review-ops.ts`. Two distinct defects combine to produce the wrong message. ### Defect 1: `runGh()` swallows stderr entirely Lines 35-44: ```typescript function runGh(args, cwd, ghBin): Promise<{ ok: boolean; stdout: string }> { return new Promise(resolve => { execFile( ghBin || 'gh', args, { cwd, env: ghEnv(ghBin), windowsHide: true, timeout: 30_000, maxBuffer: 8 * 1024 * 1024 }, (err, stdout) => resolve({ ok: !err, stdout: String(stdout || '') }) ) }) } ``` `execFile`'s callback receives `(err, stdout, stderr)`. This code destructures only `(err, stdout)` and discards stderr. By the time the caller throws, every useful error string (`gh`'s actual error message) is gone. ### Defect 2: `reviewCreatePr()` chains push + create with a swallowed push error, then attributes the failure to create Lines 765-779: ```typescript async function reviewCreatePr(repoPath, gitBin, ghBin) { const cwd = resolveRequestedPathForIpc(repoPath, { purpose: 'Review create PR' }) await reviewPush(repoPath, gitBin).catch(() => undefined) // ← push failure swallowed const created = await runGh(['pr', 'create', '--fill'], cwd, ghBin) if (!created.ok) { throw new Error('gh pr create failed (is gh installed and authenticated?)') // ← static message } ... } ``` Two issues: 1. `reviewPush(...)` failures are silently caught (`.catch(() => undefined)`). When push fails — the most common real-world reason a subsequent `gh pr create` will fail — the cause is lost. The function proceeds to `gh pr create`, which then fails for a derived reason, and the toast still says "gh pr create failed". 2. The thrown `Error` is a hard-coded string with no stderr attached. Even if `runGh` returned stderr, this throw drops it. ### Note on the surrounding infrastructure For context, the file does have some prior art for handling this correctly: - `resolveGhBinary()` (main.ts:2406) — caches a resolved path with a Homebrew/PATH fallback (added because GUI-launched Electron apps inherit a minimal PATH). So `ghBin` itself is generally correct; `gh` is being invoked. The toast text was written as if `gh` weren't there at all. - `ghEnv()` (git-review-ops.ts:25) — also explicitly augments PATH for the same reason. Both pieces of infrastructure say "we know GUI apps have a minimal PATH, we compensate"; the error toast text doesn't reflect this. ## Proposed Fix A minimal change that preserves the public API and fixes the message. Suggested patch: ```diff -function runGh(args, cwd, ghBin): Promise<{ ok: boolean; stdout: string }> { - return new Promise(resolve => { - execFile( - ghBin || 'gh', - args, - { cwd, env: ghEnv(ghBin), windowsHide: true, timeout: 30_000, maxBuffer: 8 * 1024 * 1024 }, - (err, stdout) => resolve({ ok: !err, stdout: String(stdout || '') }) - ) - }) -} +function runGh(args, cwd, ghBin): Promise<{ ok: boolean; stdout: string; stderr: string; code: number | null }> { + return new Promise(resolve => { + execFile( + ghBin || 'gh', + args, + { cwd, env: ghEnv(ghBin), windowsHide: true, timeout: 30_000, maxBuffer: 8 * 1024 * 1024 }, + (err, stdout, stderr) => + resolve({ + ok: !err, + stdout: String(stdout || ''), + stderr: String(stderr || ''), + code: err && typeof err.code === 'number' ? err.code : null, + }) + ) + }) +} async function reviewCreatePr(repoPath, gitBin, ghBin) { const cwd = resolveRequestedPathForIpc(repoPath, { purpose: 'Review create PR' }) - await reviewPush(repoPath, gitBin).catch(() => undefined) + // Surface push errors distinctly so the user can fix the push before retrying, + // instead of having the toast blame `gh pr create`. + try { + await reviewPush(repoPath, gitBin) + } catch (pushErr) { + const pushMsg = pushErr instanceof Error ? pushErr.message : String(pushErr || 'push failed') + throw new Error(`Push failed: ${pushMsg}`) + } const created = await runGh(['pr', 'create', '--fill'], cwd, ghBin) if (!created.ok) { - throw new Error('gh pr create failed (is gh installed and authenticated?)') + const tail = (created.stderr || '').trim().split('\n').filter(Boolean).slice(-3).join(' · ') || '(no stderr)' + throw new Error(`gh pr create failed: ${tail}`) } const url = created.stdout.trim().split('\n').filter(Boolean).pop() || '' return { url } } ``` Also update any other `runGh` call sites in the same file (`reviewShipInfo`, `reviewFetchPrComment`, `reviewPrList`) to consume `stderr` if they currently swallow it. A `git grep -n "runGh(" apps/desktop/electron/git-review-ops.ts` confirms five call sites. A defensive belt-and-braces improvement: have `resolveGhBinary()` also verify the resolved path with `fs.accessSync(p, fs.constants.X_OK)` so the toast can say "gh binary at /opt/homebrew/bin/gh is not executable" when that's the real reason, instead of misleadingly asking the user to install gh. ## Operating System macOS 26.4.1 (Apple Silicon, `/opt/homebrew/bin/gh`) ## Hermes Version ``` $ hermes version Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (2026.8.13) · upstream 7095e23e · local 5d526de2 (+1 carried commit) ``` ## Debug Report Local reproduction only; no remote debug paste needed because the bug is fully characterized from source. The affected file is committed at `56526bc0d3` on `main` and was last touched by commit `39d09453f9` ("feat(desktop): ts-ify everything", ethernet8023, 2026-06-29) which created the file. For developers wanting to reproduce locally without the GUI, the equivalent shell command is: ```bash gh pr create --fill --repo <owner>/<repo> ``` in a branch state that gh rejects. The Desktop app's `runGh` wrapper around this same call discards stderr and throws a hard-coded message — so the bug is independent of whether the user can run `gh pr create` from their terminal. ## Additional Logs / Traceback The Desktop app does not log `runGh`'s stderr to the main process log either; nothing currently surfaces it. A useful follow-up would be `console.error('[gh]', created.stderr)` in the catch path before re-throwing, so the Electron main log captures the real reason for users who are debugging via logs. ## Proposed Fix See "Proposed Fix" section above. Ready to submit as a PR if maintainers agree the API change to `runGh` (adding `stderr` and `code` to its return shape) is acceptable. The change is backwards compatible because `runGh` is file-local. --- ## Labels (suggested) - `bug` - `area/desktop` - `comp/review-pane` ## Willingness to submit a PR - [x] Yes — happy to submit a PR with the proposed patch, scoped to `git-review-ops.ts` only. - [ ] No --- ## Pre-flight checklist before posting - [ ] Re-confirm issue title (currently `[Bug]: Desktop Review pane "Create PR" always reports generic "is gh installed and authenticated?" even when gh is fine`) - [ ] Re-confirm labels (`bug` / `area/desktop` / `comp/review-pane` — adjust if the repo's label set differs) - [ ] Run `gh issue create --repo NousResearch/hermes-agent --title "..." --body-file <this.md> --label bug --label area/desktop --label comp/review-pane` - [ ] Confirm URL lands and copy into issue log

signals.title: [Bug]: Windows update frequently fails / partial updates block runtime repair (broken Git trampolines + venv python.exe missing + self-lock)
signals.text: ### Bug Description Title: Windows update frequently fails / partial updates block runtime repair (broken Git trampolines + venv python.exe missing + self-lock) Labels: bug, Windows, update, installer, high-priority Body: Summary On Windows, hermes update often stalls or only partially completes and requires manual recovery. Root causes are three interacting platform issues: Hermes-bundled and system Git installs can be 46KB trampoline launchers that fail with "BUG (fork bomb)" and do not re-exec git-core correctly. A partial update/venv recreate can leave the venv without a console interpreter (venv\Scripts\python.exe), leaving only pythonw.exe. That breaks uv-style trampolines (error: "uv trampoline failed to canonicalize script path"). Running the update from hermes.exe (or the venv python) self-locks the launcher/venv files, preventing the update from quarantining/replacing runtime files (e.g., managed Python runtime and SQLite), so the final runtime repair step fails. Observed behavior Update fetch may succeed (or partially succeed via ZIP fallback) but the final quarantine/replace step fails with a file lock because hermes.exe (the running process that launched the update) still holds the executable and/or venv python open. git --version returns "BUG (fork bomb)" (46KB trampoline output) because PATH resolves to broken trampolines (bin\git.exe or cmd\git.exe). The real git binary exists at mingw64\libexec\git-core\git.exe (≈4.4 MB) and works when invoked directly. After a failed/partial update, venv still contains site-packages but no python.exe, so uv-trampoline launchers fail to run Hermes. Manual recovery required: prepend mingw64\libexec\git-core to PATH and set GIT_EXEC_PATH to that dir (session-only), and re-run the update driven by SYSTEM Python (not hermes.exe). Example that repaired my installation: $env:GIT_EXEC_PATH="C:\Program Files\Git\mingw64\libexec\git-core" 𝑒 𝑛 𝑣 : 𝑃 𝐴 𝑇 𝐻 = " 𝐶 : \Program 𝐹 𝑖 𝑙 𝑒 𝑠 \Git \mingw 64 \libexec \git − 𝑐 𝑜 𝑟 𝑒 ; " + env:PATH="C:\ProgramFiles\Git\mingw64\libexec\git−core;"+env:PATH & "C:\Users<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python313\python.exe" -c "import sys; sys.argv=['hermes','update']; from hermes_cli.main import main; main()" After doing the above, update completed, venv recreated, dependencies reinstalled, and managed Python runtime updated (SQLite fixed). Why this is critical Non-technical users will be left with broken installs or will need lengthy support sessions. Partial update that cannot replace runtime leaves Hermes in an inconsistent state (old vulnerable SQLite still present until manual fix). The problem is reproducible on Windows when trampolines are present and when updates attempt runtime replacement while the launcher is running. Reproduction checklist On Windows, install Hermes (bundled PortableGit in AppData\Local\hermes\git). Ensure bin\git.exe and cmd\git.exe trampolines exist but their reexec target is broken or not found (or simulate by altering PATH so trampolines resolve first while git-core is intact). Run hermes update normally via hermes.exe. Observe: git calls fail ("BUG (fork bomb)") or are intercepted by trampoline guard. Update may proceed through ZIP fallback but fails when attempting to quarantine/replace hermes.exe (file lock). Verify venv\Scripts\python.exe may be absent if a venv recreation occurred in the partially-applied update. Fix by running update from a system Python process with GIT_EXEC_PATH and PATH pointed at mingw64\libexec\git-core — observe success. Exact environment & artifacts (from my run) Hermes agent path: C:\Users\Seth\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent System Python: 3.13.15 (C:\Users\Seth\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python313) Broken trampoline size: ~46 KB (bin\git.exe, cmd\git.exe) Real git-core binary: C:\Program Files\Git\mingw64\libexec\git-core\git.exe (≈4.38 MB), works when called directly Errors observed: "uv trampoline failed to canonicalize script path" "BUG (fork bomb)" Update blocked due to file lock when attempting to quarantine/replace hermes.exe Root-cause diagnosis (concise) The launcher/trampoline model (small launcher that reexecs a larger git-core) is brittle if PATH/env are altered or helper files are missing; trampolines emit a fork-bomb guard and fail. The update flow runs destructive steps (quarantine/replace managed runtime) from inside the running launcher process (hermes.exe), which causes file locks on Windows and prevents atomic replacement. Venv recreation isn't atomic and can leave an incomplete venv with site-packages but missing python.exe, breaking launchers that expect console interpreter to exist. Recommended fixes (prioritized) High priority (reduce support pain immediately) Change the update flow to avoid performing runtime replacement/quarantine steps from inside the running launcher. On Windows, spawn an external system-python helper (or a short-lived installer process) that performs the replace/rename operations so hermes.exe and venv\Scripts\python.exe are not held open during replacement. Add an explicit pre-update healthcheck and fail-fast with clear troubleshooting guidance: Confirm git --version returns a valid version; if it appears to be a trampoline, probe mingw64\libexec\git-core\git.exe and prefer that in-session for the update. Confirm venv\Scripts\python.exe exists. If missing, either recreate the venv in an atomic safe way or require update to be run via system Python automatically. Provide a documented --use-system-python (or --no-self-lock) flag that triggers the system-Python-driven update sequence automatically. Medium priority (robustness) Provide a user config option (e.g. hermes.git_path) to point the updater at a specific git binary if the PATH-resolved git is unreliable. Make the venv recreate process atomic — create a new venv directory then replace/rename it into place only after it is fully populated, to avoid leaving a half-recreated venv. Improve the ZIP fallback/update logic to prefer using real git-core when present, rather than relying on PATH-resolved bare git. Low priority / ergonomics When quarantine/replace fails due to file lock, print a clear actionable message: e.g., "Update partially applied. To finish runtime repair, re-run this update from system Python: ." Offer a --finish-update helper that runs the system-Python-driven remainder. Add logging/telemetry that distinguishes "partial update applied, quarantine failed due to file lock" so support can triage quickly. Consider shipping a small robust shim for PortableGit that correctly sets GIT_EXEC_PATH for its subprocesses and is tolerant to PATH manipulations. Suggested minimal fix patch (developer guidance) Implement update orchestration like: Pre-flight: detect if runtime replacement is required. If yes: launch a system-Python helper process (or elevated updater) that: Terminates/ensures no hermes.exe or venv python processes are running Performs the replace/quarantine atomically Restarts the user agent if appropriate Alternatively, provide hermes update --use-system-python which does the above. Attachments / logs to help debugging Sample transcript with the exact commands that worked for me: $env:GIT_EXEC_PATH="C:\Program Files\Git\mingw64\libexec\git-core" 𝑒 𝑛 𝑣 : 𝑃 𝐴 𝑇 𝐻 = " 𝐶 : \Program 𝐹 𝑖 𝑙 𝑒 𝑠 \Git \mingw 64 \libexec \git − 𝑐 𝑜 𝑟 𝑒 ; " + env:PATH="C:\ProgramFiles\Git\mingw64\libexec\git−core;"+env:PATH & "C:\Users<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python313\python.exe" -c "import sys; sys.argv=['hermes','update']; from hermes_cli.main import main; main()" Sizes and paths for trampolines vs real binaries (46KB vs 4.4MB) Observed hermes doctor outputs before/after showing SQLite moved from 3.50.4 → 3.53.1 after the system-Python-driven update Request Please confirm whether you can: Add a documented system-Python-driven update path or auto-fallback when runtime replacement is required. Add pre-update health checks for PATH/git and venv python presence. Provide a supported configuration option to pin the git binary used by the updater. I can provide full logs, transcripts, and help test a patch or pre-release fix. Thank you — resolving these issues will greatly reduce Windows support burden and make updates reliable for end users. (If helpful, I can also paste a 3–4 line “how to recover” snippet for docs or a one-paragraph summary for the issue title.) ### Steps to Reproduce in the body ### Expected Behavior This has happened to me after every update of the windows hermes app ### Actual Behavior takes a ton of time to fix ### Affected Component Setup / Installation ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) N/A (CLI only) ### Debug Report ```shell s ``` ### Operating System windows 11 pro ### Python Version _No response_ ### Hermes Version _No response_ ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) _No response_ ### Proposed Fix (optional) _No response_ ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

signals.title: Bot Mode: bot-to-bot reply silently drops when receiving profile has no Bot Chat session (ported from Hermes-Bot-Mode#48)
signals.text: Ported from Hermes-Bot-Mode#48 (Bug 1) — that repo is archived; Bot Mode now ships bundled (`apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/`, #87886). ## Bug — bot-to-bot reply silently drops when the receiving profile has no "Bot Chat" session yet **Steps (reporter's, v0.20.1 desktop):** Bot A messages Bot B via `hermes -p <B> chat ...`. Bot B replies with `hermes -p <B> chat -c "Bot Chat" -q "<reply>"` (background send). If profile B has never had a "Bot Chat" session, the reply never lands — no error, no delivery. Works only after manually creating/renaming a "Bot Chat" session on the receiving profile. **Expected:** delivery creates the session, or a clear error says it must exist. **Likely mechanism:** the gateway `session.create` lazy-session trap — RPC-created sessions write no state.db row until the first message, so CLI `chat -c "<title>"` can't resolve them; conversely a CLI targeting a title that only exists as a lazy session finds nothing. The bundled plugin gained canonical-chat creation/empty-recovery paths (see `canonical-chat-creation.test.mjs`, `canonical-chat-empty-recovery.test.mjs`), so first verify whether current main still reproduces before fixing. **Prior art:** frozen PR Hermes-Bot-Mode#61 ("pre-flight canonical Bot Chat before @mention handoffs") attempted the plugin-side half — worth salvaging its approach if the repro stands. Bug 2 from the original issue ('restore checkpoint' blocks the composer) is already tracked here as #86795.

signals.title: feat(desktop): composer @ autocomplete should offer Bot Mode agents (ported from Hermes-Bot-Mode#43)
signals.text: Ported from Hermes-Bot-Mode#43 — that repo is archived; Bot Mode now ships bundled and default-on (#87886). ## Feature — composer `@` autocomplete should offer Bot Mode agents The composer's `@` autocomplete only lists filesystem references. Bot handles are recognized by the Bot Mode middleware when fully typed (e.g. `@researcher`), but never offered as completions — users must already know the exact handle. Now that Bot Mode is bundled and the roster is multi-source (#86875 + #87886), the completion set should be the union agent roster, including `@name-device` handles for duplicated profile names across registered connections. Suggestion source likely belongs in `src/store/composer-suggestions.ts` alongside the existing providers, fed from the same roster the Bots panel uses.

signals.title: Design: per-task multi-agent workflow — IM-style task trace + reliable execution (ported from Hermes-Bot-Mode#108)
signals.text: Ported from Hermes-Bot-Mode#108 — that repo is archived; Bot Mode development moved in-tree (#87886). ## Design question — per-task multi-agent workflow (IM-style task trace + reliable execution) Original ask (design/roadmap, not a patch request): should Bot Mode grow a per-task workflow with 1. **Trace:** opening one task shows the agent-to-agent DMs *that task* caused, chat-app style (conversation list + bubble transcripts), instead of reconstructing the job from each bot's canonical Bot Chat. 2. **Reliable execution:** the pipeline runs in order and finishes/fails cleanly — not dependent on a lead bot's SOUL "remembering" the next hop; a later step must not start when an earlier one failed. Pattern: `human → A (front desk) → B → C`, with the human only ever talking to A. Related in-tree work to weigh in the answer: group chats in the bundled plugin, frozen Hermes-Bot-Mode#102 (Group Agents / team orchestration), frozen Hermes-Bot-Mode#106 (pane control surface), #86135 (CEO delegate_task visible C-suite conversation), and the kanban plugin's task model. Full original text: https://github.com/NousResearch/Hermes-Bot-Mode/issues/108

signals.title: [Bug]: /skill slash invoke fails when skills.external_dirs is the package root
signals.text: ## Bug Description Desktop (and any other `command.dispatch` surface) advertises installed skills as `/<skill>` slash commands, then fails to invoke them when `skills.external_dirs` contains the **skill package root** rather than a parent directory of many skills. The user-visible error is: ```text /wayfinder : error: not a quick/plugin/bundle/skill command: wayfinder ``` The skill **is** installed and enabled. `hermes skills list` shows it. Desktop’s `/` picker shows it. `skill_view(name)` in a normal chat turn works. Only the slash-invocation path fails, and the error text is wrong: dispatch found the skill, then failed to load it. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure a custom skill as its own external dir (common when a repo is a library of one-skill packages): ```yaml skills: external_dirs: - /path/to/my-skills/wayfinder # this directory contains SKILL.md ``` 2. Confirm the skill is enabled (`hermes skills list` / Desktop `/` picker shows `/wayfinder`). 3. In Hermes Desktop, type `/`, pick the skill, send `/wayfinder`. 4. Observe the system line: `not a quick/plugin/bundle/skill command: wayfinder`. A parent-dir layout does **not** hit this: ```yaml skills: external_dirs: - /path/to/my-skills # contains wayfinder/SKILL.md ``` Skills that live under `~/.hermes/skills/<name>` also work, because the relative path is `name` rather than `.`. ## Expected Behavior `/wayfinder` should expand the skill and submit it as a normal skill-invocation turn, same as typing `wayfinder` in prose (which goes through `skill_view("wayfinder")`). If load still fails, the error should say the skill was found but the payload failed to load — not that it is not a skill command. ## Actual Behavior Desktop routes `/wayfinder` through `slash.exec` → `command.dispatch`. Dispatch finds `/wayfinder` in `scan_skill_commands()`, calls `build_skill_invocation_message()`, gets `None`, then falls through to: ```text not a quick/plugin/bundle/skill command: wayfinder ``` (`tui_gateway/methods_tools.py`, the final `_err(..., 4018, ...)` after the skill-load `if msg:` block.) ## Affected Component - Skills (skill loading, skill hub, skill guard) - Other: Desktop composer slash picker / `command.dispatch` / TUI gateway ## Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) - N/A (CLI only) — reproduced on Desktop against a local/remote TUI gateway, not a messaging adapter ## Debug Report Skipped `hermes debug share`. This is a deterministic source-level bug; a debug upload would ship private config and skill paths without adding a repro. The live error string and the call chain below are sufficient. ## Operating System - Gateway host: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (Linux 6.19.8-surface-3 x86_64) - Desktop client: Windows (Hermes Desktop, remote to that gateway) ## Python Version 3.11.15 ## Hermes Version Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3) ## Root Cause Analysis `scan_skill_commands()` correctly registers the skill. `command.dispatch` then loads it via the **absolute `skill_dir`**, not the skill name: ```python # agent/skill_commands.py — build_skill_invocation_message() loaded = _load_skill_payload(skill_info["skill_dir"], task_id=task_id) ``` `_load_skill_payload()` runs that path through `normalize_skill_lookup_name()` so `skill_view()` can accept it. That helper treats every `skills.external_dirs` entry as a trusted **root** and returns `path.relative_to(root)`. When the configured external dir **is** the skill package: ```text identifier = /path/to/my-skills/wayfinder trusted root = /path/to/my-skills/wayfinder # same path relative_to(root) → "." ``` `skill_view(".")` is not a valid skill name (`_skill_lookup_path_error` / lookup miss). `_load_skill_payload` returns `None`. Dispatch swallows that and reports “not a skill command.” Relevant code: - `agent/skill_utils.py` — `normalize_skill_lookup_name()` (`relative_to` over `get_external_skills_dirs()`) - `agent/skill_commands.py` — `_load_skill_payload()` / `build_skill_invocation_message()` - `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py` — `command.dispatch` skill branch, then the generic 4018 - `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/slash.ts` — `/<unknown>` is treated as an extension skill and sent to `slash.exec` / `command.dispatch` This is not Desktop-only. Any surface that invokes via `build_skill_invocation_message(skill_dir=...)` will fail for the same layout. Desktop is just the surface that advertises `/` as the way to invoke skills. ## Proposed Fix Any one of these is enough; the first is the smallest: 1. In `normalize_skill_lookup_name()`, if `relative_to(root)` is `"."`, return the package directory name (`identifier_path.name`) instead of `"."`. 2. Or have `build_skill_invocation_message()` pass `skill_info["name"]` into `_load_skill_payload()`, not `skill_dir`. 3. In `command.dispatch`, if the skill key exists but `build_skill_invocation_message()` returns `None`, return a distinct error (`failed to load skill payload: {name}`) instead of the generic 4018. A regression test should cover `skills.external_dirs: [/abs/path/to/<skill>]` (package root, not parent) and assert `/<skill>` builds a non-empty invocation message. ## Workaround Type the skill name **without** `/`. That uses `skill_view("<name>")` and works. ## Are you willing to submit a PR for this? Not in this report. Happy to follow up with a focused PR if wanted.

signals.title: [Bug] Shift+Space still leaks raw CSI bytes into the buffer on main — follow-up to #86866
signals.text: Follow-up to #86866, which I'm unable to reopen (no permission) but which I believe wasn't actually fixed. Thanks for the quick turnaround on #87511/#87630 — the Ctrl+letter side works great. But Shift+Space is still broken on bab7be3 (main): the mapping from those PRs is on disk and the parser half works, yet the raw Shift+Space sequence still lands in the buffer. Repro (live install, prompt_toolkit 3.0.52, tmux over SSH, set -g escape-time 0): the script below installs the alias functions the same way cli.py:87-91 does, then feeds key sequences through a real Vt100Parser → Buffer: ``` python import asyncio, sys sys.path.insert(0, "/path/to/hermes-agent") # adjust from prompt_toolkit.buffer import Buffer from prompt_toolkit.layout import Layout, HSplit, Window, BufferControl from prompt_toolkit import Application from prompt_toolkit.input import create_pipe_input from hermes_cli import pt_input_extras as p p.install_shift_enter_alias(); p.install_ctrl_enter_alias() p.install_cmd_backspace_alias(); p.install_modify_other_keys_aliases() p.install_ignored_terminal_sequences() CASES = { "Ctrl+K xterm": "\x1b[27;5;107~", "Shift+Space xterm": "\x1b[27;2;32~", "Shift+Space kitty": "\x1b[32;2u", "plain space": " ", } async def probe(label, payload): buf = Buffer() with create_pipe_input() as inp: app = Application(layout=Layout(HSplit([Window(BufferControl(buf))])), input=inp) run_task = asyncio.ensure_future(app.run_async()) await asyncio.sleep(0.2) inp.send_text("ab") inp.send_text(payload) inp.send_text("cd") await asyncio.sleep(0.4) result = buf.text app.exit() try: await asyncio.wait_for(run_task, 2) except Exception: pass print(f"{label:22s} -> buffer={result!r}") async def main(): for label, payload in CASES.items(): await probe(label, payload) asyncio.run(main()) ``` Output on bab7be3: ``` Ctrl+K xterm -> buffer='abcd' Shift+Space xterm -> buffer='ab\x1b[27;2;32~cd' <-- leaks Shift+Space kitty -> buffer='ab\x1b[32;2ucd' <-- leaks plain space -> buffer='ab cd' ``` What I believe is happening: Vt100Parser._call_handler (vt100_parser.py:191) builds KeyPress(key, match.group(0)), so the KeyPress key is correctly mapped to ' ' by the new alias, but the data field still carries the full raw prefix. The character-insert binding (key_binding/bindings/basic.py:232) inserts event.data — the raw bytes — rather than the mapped key. For a normal space both fields are ' ' so it's invisible; for the extended sequence, data is the escape text and that's what gets inserted. (This is the pitfall the original issue mentioned: a bare " " mapping needs a handler that actually inserts the space.) Test note: test_shift_space_inserts_space asserts on key_press.key == ' ', which is parser output only — so it passes even though the buffer-level behavior leaks. A test that checks buffer contents after processing would catch this class of regression. A possible direction (either): 1. Map the token to a dedicated unused Keys member (e.g. Keys.ControlAt) plus one @kb.add handler that calls event.current_buffer.insert_text(' ') — sidesteps the data field, same pattern as the Ctrl/Alt bindings; or 2. Normalize the sequence to a bare space at parser level before KeyPress construction. Happy to help verify a fix. Thanks!

signals.title: docs(windows): gateway troubleshooting recommends HERMES_GATEWAY_FORCE_STARTUP, which no code reads
signals.text: ## Summary The "Gateway won't stay running after restart" troubleshooting entry in `website/docs/user-guide/windows-native.md` gives three instructions, and all three are wrong against current `main`. The most serious tells the user to set an environment variable that no code reads. Verified against `origin/main` today; all cited files are byte-identical to upstream in my checkout, so none of this rests on a local modification. ### 1. `HERMES_GATEWAY_FORCE_STARTUP` does not exist > …or fall back to the Startup-folder path by uninstalling and reinstalling with `HERMES_GATEWAY_FORCE_STARTUP=1`. ``` $ git grep -c HERMES_GATEWAY_FORCE_STARTUP origin/main origin/main:website/docs/user-guide/windows-native.md:1 origin/main:website/i18n/zh-Hans/.../windows-native.md:1 ``` Two hits, both documentation. Nothing reads the variable — there is no env var, CLI flag, or `install()` parameter that forces the Startup-folder path. `hermes gateway install` exposes only `--start-on-login`, `--no-start-on-login`, and the suppressed `--elevated-handoff`. The fallback is **automatic only**, and it engages solely on schtasks *stderr*: ```python def _should_fall_back(code: int, detail: str) -> bool: return code == 124 or bool(_FALLBACK_PATTERNS.search(detail or "")) ``` **Why this matters more than a stale flag:** the advice targets precisely the one case where the automatic fallback provably cannot engage. The paragraph's own premise is that schtasks *registered successfully* (clean stderr → no pattern matches) but group policy is blocking the `ONLOGON` trigger. A user following this sets a variable nothing reads, uninstalls, reinstalls, gets an identical non-firing Scheduled Task, and is left with no documented recovery for a gateway that silently never starts at login. ### 2. The fallback writes a `.vbs`, not a `cmd.exe` shortcut Step 2 of the same page describes the fallback as writing a `start /min cmd.exe /d /c <wrapper>` shortcut. It writes a VBScript launched via `wscript.exe`: ```python def get_startup_entry_path() -> Path: _assert_windows() return _startup_dir() / f"{_sanitize_filename(get_task_name())}.vbs" ``` `_install_startup_entry` also actively deletes the legacy `.cmd`. The `cmd.exe` layer was removed deliberately — a console allocated at logon receives `CTRL_CLOSE_EVENT`, killing a half-initialised gateway with `STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT`, which Task Scheduler records as a *user cancel* so `RestartOnFailure` never fires. ### 3. The task name in the diagnostic command is wrong The page tells users to run `schtasks /Query /TN HermesGateway /V /FO LIST`, but the task is named `Hermes_Gateway` (`_TASK_NAME_DEFAULT`, per-profile `Hermes_Gateway_<profile>`). As written the command returns "task does not exist", in the middle of troubleshooting a task that does. ## Suggested fix Item 1 needs a maintainer decision, which is why this is an issue rather than a PR: either drop the sentence, or implement the override. The module already has an env-driven install-choice helper (`_install_choice_from_env`), so wiring one in looks small if the escape hatch is considered worth having. Items 2 and 3 are straightforward doc corrections. Happy to send a PR for those two alone if that's useful — say the word and I'll scope it to the English page plus the zh-Hans mirror. ## Environment Native Windows 11, gateway installed via `hermes gateway install` (Scheduled Task `Hermes_Gateway` + `wscript.exe` → `.vbs` → venv `python.exe -m hermes_cli.main gateway run`). _🤖 Reported with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

signals.title: feat(telegram): support secure Bot API Guest Queries
signals.text: ## Summary - upgrade `python-telegram-bot` to 22.8 for Bot API Guest Query support - add a distinct, explicit `allow_guest_queries` opt-in that remains off by default and does not overload existing `guest_mode` - preserve Telegram user authorization and explicitly enforce configured chat/topic/own-message/trigger gates - rate-limit accepted intake per sender/chat with bounded state and deduplicate repeated `guest_query_id` updates - isolate each query in a synthetic one-shot session lane - deliver exactly one formatted, length-bounded text answer through `answerGuestQuery` - suppress typing, streaming, progress, media/file sends, TTS, normal-send fallback, and duplicate final delivery - fail closed for interactive clarification and command approval: no normal `sendMessage`; clarification returns control to the agent and approval-required operations are denied - block the cross-channel `send_message` tool—including list/send/react/unreact—during Guest Query turns so it cannot bypass `answerGuestQuery` - return a clear text-only answer for unsupported guest media/location payloads - document configuration, limitations, and full-tool trust implications in English and Chinese ## Security model Bot API Guest Queries can originate from chats where the bot is not a member, so support is disabled unless the operator explicitly enables `allow_guest_queries` (or `TELEGRAM_ALLOW_GUEST_QUERIES=true`). Enabling it does not authorize new users: normal Telegram user authorization still runs, configured `allowed_chats` is enforced explicitly for PTB's special `sender` chat type, and topic/own-message/trigger gates remain active. Accepted Guest Queries otherwise use the same configured agent and tools as other authorized Telegram turns. They are session-isolated but are not a general reduced-permission tool sandbox. The cross-channel `send_message` tool is blocked to preserve the one-shot delivery boundary. The one-shot transport cannot host interactive clarification or approval buttons; operations requiring approval are denied automatically. ## Configuration ```yaml gateway: platforms: telegram: extra: allow_guest_queries: true guest_query_rate_limit_per_minute: 5 ``` The rate limit is per sender/chat, clamped to 1–60 accepted queries per minute. State is bounded to prevent unbounded key growth. ## Verification Rebased onto current `main`. The sole conflict was in `pyproject.toml`; resolution preserves upstream `aiohttp==3.14.3` and this PR's PTB 22.8 requirement. - comprehensive focused selection: **62 files, 626 passed, 0 failed** - all `tests/gateway/test_telegram*.py` - changed proxy/run/recovery modules - approval and clarification contract suites - project metadata/pin invariants - real PTB 22.8 `Update.de_json()` Guest Message intake probe: passed - adjacent `test_platform_base.py`: **84 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed**; the same credential-path test fails identically on untouched current `main` and is pre-existing - `uv lock --check`: passed; PTB resolves to 22.8 and upstream aiohttp remains 3.14.3 - Ruff, Python compilation, static security scan, and `git diff --check`: passed ## Review follow-up This revision addresses the prior findings: handler ordering; explicit default-off trust-boundary gating; user/chat/topic scope; rate limiting and deduplication; long-answer formatting and bounded delivery; one-shot runner/session propagation; suppression of normal-send auxiliary paths; fail-closed approval/clarification handling; Guest media/location behavior; and lazy-dependency pin consistency.

signals.title: fix(fallback): honor explicit api_mode on fallback_providers entries
signals.text: ## Problem `try_activate_fallback()` in `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` re-derives `api_mode` for a fallback entry purely from provider name / base_url heuristics — it never reads the `api_mode` field the user explicitly set on that `fallback_providers` config entry. For a custom proxy/endpoint whose host doesn't match any of the heuristics (not `api.anthropic.com`, not `api.openai.com`, not Azure, not Bedrock), the code silently discards an explicitly configured `api_mode: anthropic_messages` and falls through to the `chat_completions` default. ### Symptom Observed in production with a custom Anthropic-compatible proxy configured as a fallback: ```yaml fallback_providers: - provider: custom:MyProxy model: claude-sonnet-4-6 api_key: ${MY_API_KEY} base_url: https://my-proxy.example.com api_mode: anthropic_messages ``` When the primary provider hit a 429 and the agent switched to this fallback, the request went to `POST /chat/completions` with a `Bearer` auth header (chat_completions wire format) instead of `POST /v1/messages` with an `x-api-key` header (the configured anthropic_messages format). The proxy doesn't serve `/chat/completions` at all, so it returned its frontend's HTML 404 page instead of a JSON API error, and the whole fallback chain failed after 3 retries — even though the endpoint and credentials were both valid. ## Fix Read `fb.get("api_mode")` first. If the config entry specifies one, use it as-is (it's authoritative — the user is telling us the wire protocol for an endpoint the heuristics can't classify from the URL alone). Only fall back to the existing provider/base_url heuristics when the entry didn't specify `api_mode`. ## Testing - `python3 -m py_compile agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` — syntax OK - Verified against my own multi-profile Hermes setup: reproduced the 404-on-fallback failure with an `api_mode: anthropic_messages` custom fallback provider, applied the fix, restarted the gateway, and confirmed the fallback path now correctly resolves to `anthropic_messages` instead of defaulting to `chat_completions`. - No test suite changes — did not have time to write a unit test covering `try_activate_fallback`'s api_mode resolution path; happy to add one if requested.

signals.title: fix(gateway): keep background delegation results in parent turn
signals.text: ## Bug description A gateway `/background` task could call `delegate_task`, return an interim response, and close its temporary `bg_*` session before the delegated batch finished. The children later completed, but their result could not re-enter the permanently closed parent session. ## Root cause The temporary `/background` task inherited the originating live chat's async-delivery capability. That capability is valid for the persistent live chat, but not for the finite background agent turn: once the turn returns and its agent closes, it has no durable consumer for a detached completion. ## Fix - mark only the copied `/background` asyncio task context as unable to receive late async completions - reuse the existing finite-session `delegate_task` fallback so the aggregate returns while the background parent is active - preserve concurrent child fan-out - preserve ordinary live-chat asynchronous delegation because the originating context is unchanged - add regression coverage for copied-task and caller-context isolation ## Verification on current `main` - focused and adjacent background/delegation suites: 32 passed - independent review: approved; no security, concurrency, or context-isolation blockers - Ruff: passed - Python compilation: passed - `git diff --check`: passed ## Risk Low. The change sets an existing `ContextVar` capability only inside the asyncio task created specifically for `/background`; it reuses established finite-session behavior rather than adding a new delivery path.

signals.title: feat(gateway): add Unix socket dispatcher forwarding
signals.text: ## What Add opt-in Unix socket forwarding so the gateway can delegate configured slash commands to an external dispatcher service instead of routing them through the agent loop. - `gateway/dispatcher_protocol.py`: wire-protocol dataclasses (Envelope, status codes, ops) - `gateway/dispatcher_client.py`: async Unix-socket client with retry, timeout, lock-safe connect/close - `gateway/run.py`: wiring in `_handle_message` between drain check and quick-commands cascade - `gateway/config.py`: dispatcher_socket and dispatcher_commands in GatewayConfig - Tests: real asyncio Unix socket server fixture, covers connection lifecycle, retry, timeout, status code propagation, concurrency ## Context This is the dispatcher forwarding functionality originally in #57112, which was closed in favor of #65688. The dispatcher code was later removed from #65688 to keep it scoped to Weixin session detection (per review feedback). This PR revives the dispatcher forwarding with all original review findings fixed: 1. **Gate forwarding with `_check_slash_access`** — non-admin users can no longer invoke configured dispatcher commands (security fix) 2. **Catch `LimitOverrunError`** — oversized responses converted to `DispatcherConnectionError` for non-fatal fallback 3. **Config-only socket path** — no env var fallback, complies with env-var-for-config policy ## Config Dispatcher is configured via `config.yaml`: ```yaml dispatcher: socket: /run/harness/dispatcher.sock commands: [echo, research, forge, ashare, replay, log] ``` When dispatcher.socket is not set, dispatcher commands are handled locally instead of forwarded. ## Related - #57112 (closed) — original dispatcher PR - #65688 (open) — Weixin stale session detection (dispatcher code removed from this PR) - #75268 (closed) — previous version, closed by sweeper for env-var-for-config policy - #76792 (closed) — previous version, closed by sweeper for env-var-for-config policy ## Testing - 39 unit tests: connection lifecycle, retry behavior, timeout, status code propagation, asyncio.Lock concurrency, access control gate, config validation - `pytest tests/gateway/test_dispatcher_client.py -q` — 39/39 pass - CLI forge review: deepseek-omni backend, 3 passes Signed-off-by: Minxi Hou <houminxi@gmail.com>
