signal.title: hermes chat -q (single-query) sessions never finalize — ended_at stays NULL, unbounded session leak
signal.text: ## Summary `hermes chat -q` / `hermes chat --query` (non-interactive single-query mode) creates a session row but never stamps `ended_at` / `end_reason` on exit. Because `hermes sessions prune` only deletes rows where `ended_at IS NOT NULL`, these sessions are invisible to pruning and accumulate without bound. ## Regression (second occurrence) - Originally fixed in v0.18.0 (`_finalize_single_query` in `cli.py` → `agent.close()`). - Regressed again in the v0.20.x one-shot refactor, which moved single-query execution into `hermes_cli/oneshot.py` without carrying the `end_session()` finalization. ## Reproduction ```bash hermes chat -q "Reply with exactly the single word: ok" \ --quiet --model deepseek-v4-flash --provider deepseek ``` Then inspect the resulting session: ```sql SELECT id, source, model, started_at, ended_at, end_reason FROM sessions WHERE id = '<session_id>'; -- ended_at: NULL, end_reason: NULL ``` Expected: `ended_at` stamped with an `end_reason` such as `agent_close` (as the interactive CLI path does). Actual: both `NULL`. Reproduced on v0.20.1 (2026.8.13), install method git, Python 3.11.15. ## Root cause The single-query execution path is `hermes_cli/oneshot.py`. Its `finally` block (lines ~468–492) calls `agent.close()` and `session_db.close()`, but never calls `session_db.end_session()`. The comment at line ~485 states: > agent.close() calls session_db.end_session() but leaves the connection open; close it here to checkpoint the WAL before os._exit skips finalizers. …but that assertion no longer holds: - `agent/agent_init.py:1660` sets `agent._end_session_on_close = True`, yet that flag is never read anywhere in the codebase (only two assignments total; the other is `agent/background_review.py:896` setting it `False`). So `AIAgent.close()` has nothing honoring the flag. - `hermes_cli/oneshot.py` contains zero `session_db.end_session()` calls (verified by grep). For contrast, the interactive CLI path still finalizes correctly via the legacy `cli.py` god-file: `cli.py:18529` calls `self._session_db.end_session(self.agent.session_id, "cli_close")`. ## Why the regression was invisible The existing tests (`tests/cli/test_single_query_session_finalize.py`, `tests/cli/test_chat_q_exit_clear.py`) exercise `cli._finalize_single_query` — the old `cli.py` helper — not the new `hermes_cli/oneshot.py` execution path. There is no end-to-end test asserting that a real `hermes chat -q` run stamps `ended_at`. ## Impact - Every `hermes chat -q` invocation leaks one unfinalized session row. - This is the primary mode used by scripted/automated workers (e.g. our colony dispatcher spawns `hermes chat -q --quiet` on a loop), so the leak is continuous: ~6–8 rows/day in our deployment, ~580 accumulated, 542 MB `state.db`. - `hermes sessions prune` and `auto_prune` (`retention_days`) cannot reclaim these rows because they gate on `ended_at IS NOT NULL`. ## Suggested fix In `hermes_cli/oneshot.py`, finalize the session in the `finally` block — e.g. call `session_db.end_session(agent.session_id, "agent_close")` (mirroring `run_agent.py:4425`) before `session_db.close()`. Add an end-to-end test that runs a real `hermes chat -q` and asserts the resulting session row has `ended_at IS NOT NULL`, so this class of regression cannot recur silently.

signal.title: feat(web): add Indonesian (id) locale
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Adds **Bahasa Indonesia (Indonesian)** as a new UI language for the web dashboard. Indonesian is one of the world's most widely spoken languages (200+ million native speakers, Indonesia is the 4th most populous country), yet the dashboard ships English plus 16 other locales with no Indonesian. This PR adds a complete `id` locale so Indonesian-speaking users can use the dashboard in their own language. The locale is built with the existing `defineLocale` helper (`web/src/i18n/define-locale.ts`), which merges partial translations over `en`. This keeps every current and future English key available and falls back to English text where a translation is missing — rather than rendering `undefined` (the runtime `context.tsx` uses `t: TRANSLATIONS[locale]` with no fallback, so a full-object locale that lags `en` can show blank UI; `defineLocale` prevents that). ## Related Issue No issue exists for this feature. Following the contributing guide's "Search First" step, I searched issues and PRs (`gh search issues --repo NousResearch/hermes-agent "indonesia OR indonesian OR bahasa"`) — zero results, and no `id.ts` / `id` locale exists in the tree. The guide permits direct PRs without a pre-approved issue. Fixes # ## Type of Change <!-- Check the one that applies. --> - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made <!-- List the specific changes. Include file paths for code changes. --> - `web/src/i18n/id.ts` — **new**: complete Bahasa Indonesia translations for all dashboard sections (common, app, status, sessions, analytics, models, logs, cron, profiles, plugins, skills, config, env, oauth, language, theme, achievements, kanban). Built on `defineLocale` so it stays in sync with `en` automatically. - `web/src/i18n/types.ts` — added `"id"` to the `Locale` union type. - `web/src/i18n/context.tsx` — imported `id`, registered it in `TRANSLATIONS` and `LOCALE_META` (endonym: "Bahasa Indonesia"). ## How to Test <!-- Steps to verify this change works. For bugs: reproduction steps + proof that the fix works. --> 1. `cd web && npm install && npm run typecheck` — passes with 0 errors. 2. `cd web && npm run build` — builds successfully. 3. Run the dashboard (`hermes` → open Web UI), open the language picker, select **Bahasa Indonesia** — the UI renders in Indonesian. 4. Switch back to English — everything still works. ## Checklist <!-- Complete these before requesting review. --> ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`feat(web): add Indonesian (id) locale with partial translations`) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (3 files, all i18n) - [x] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — *N/A for this change (web/ only; ran `npx tsc -p . --noEmit`, `npm run build`, and web vitest instead)* - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) — *No dedicated i18n test suite exists in `web/`; the change is type-checked and built.* - [x] I've tested on my platform: Debian 13 (Linux), Node 22 ### Documentation & Housekeeping <!-- Check all that apply. It's OK to check "N/A" if a category doesn't apply to your change. --> - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A (*N/A: i18n addition, no docs describe the locale list*) - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A (*N/A: pure frontend i18n, no OS APIs*) ## Heads-up (for reviewers) - **`defineLocale` vs full-object locales.** Existing locales (`de`, `es`, `fr`, …) are full `Translations` objects and currently lag `en` by ~79 keys — because `context.tsx` does `t: TRANSLATIONS[locale]` with no runtime fallback, those missing keys render as `undefined` (blank UI). Using `defineLocale` for `id` means every key resolves (falling back to English text where untranslated), so the Indonesian UI never shows blank strings. If the project prefers all locales as full objects for consistency, `id.ts` can be expanded to a full object — happy to adjust. - **Untranslated keys**: ~45 keys intentionally remain English (proper nouns & technical terms: "Hermes Agent", "Gateway", "Cron", "Model", "Prompt", "Telegram", "Slack", "Font", "Slug", "Tenant", cron expressions, etc.) — standard practice for technical UI.

signal.title: feat(desktop): remote gateway headers for access proxies (Cloudflare Access) — salvage #74468
signal.text: ## Summary Salvages contributor PR #74468 (`feat(desktop): support remote gateway headers` by @tigercraft4, cherry-picked with authorship preserved) and completes it against current `main`, so Hermes Desktop can connect to remote gateways sitting behind access proxies such as **Cloudflare Access** — attaching `CF-Access-Client-Id` / `CF-Access-Client-Secret` (or any safe custom header) to **both the HTTP and WebSocket legs** without a local header-injecting proxy. Fixes #74466. ## Root cause Desktop had no place to store or send provider-required headers: REST probes (`/api/status`), OAuth/ticket requests (`/api/auth/ws-ticket`), and renderer WebSocket upgrades (`/api/ws`) all went out bare, so an access proxy rejected/redirected them before Hermes ever saw the request. The only workaround was a loopback proxy that injected the headers. ## Changes **Cherry-picked from #74468 (author: @tigercraft4)** — commit `97f5e552ff`: - `remote.headers` / per-profile `headers` in `connection.json`, normalized through a denylist (`Authorization`, `Cookie`, `Host`, `Origin`, `Referer`, `X-Hermes-Session-Token`, hop-by-hop/framing headers are dropped) and stored as Desktop secret envelopes (`plain`/`safeStorage`, encrypted like tokens). - HTTPS↔WSS scheme-normalized URL matching (`remoteRequestMatchesBaseUrl`) and exact-WS-URL header binding (`rememberRemoteWsHeaders`) — resolving both sweeper review blockers (direct `https:`-vs-`wss:` comparison; first-match profile scanning). - Header propagation through `fetchJson`/`fetchPublicJson`/`fetchJsonViaOauthSession`, readiness probes, ws-ticket minting, and renderer WebSocket upgrades via `webRequest.onBeforeSendHeaders`. - Unit tests + README documentation of the manual `connection.json` format. **Completion on top (this PR's second commit)** — the PR predated the v2 multi-connection registry and the two-leg connection test, so: - **v2 connections registry**: additive optional `headers` field on remote/cloud entries (`connection-registry.ts`) — normalized with the same filter, inherited on edit, treated as dial material by `connectionDialFieldsChanged` (a changed access credential recycles live backends/sockets), preserved by `normalizeRegistry`, and carried through `migrateV1ToRegistry`. **No registry version bump; v2 files written before this field load unchanged.** - **Registry dial paths**: `connectRegistryBackend` sends the entry's headers on the readiness probe, descriptor REST (`getJsonForBackend` / `fetchJsonForBackend`), and registry ws-url minting (`hermes:gateway:ws-url-for`), registering minted WS URLs so renderer upgrades get the headers injected. - **Connection tests exercise the leg they validate** (per `apps/desktop/AGENTS.md`): both `hermes:connection-config:test` and `hermes:connections:test` now send the configured headers on the HTTP status call, the ws-ticket mint, *and* the live WebSocket probe — `probeGatewayWebSocket` grew an injectable `headers` option (undici WebSocket second constructor argument). - **Settings → Connections UI**: an "Extra gateway headers" editor for remote/cloud entries (name + secret value rows; stored values surface as saved-but-hidden via `headerNames` — header *values* never cross the IPC boundary; plaintext values are encrypted on save through the same `allowPlainTextToken` seam as tokens). i18n keys added for `en` + `zh` (other locales fall back through `defineLocale`). ## #84483 (self-hosted auth_provider) — partially addressed; remainder scoped #84483 reports "Remote gateway incomplete" with no sign-in button when connecting to a gateway gated by a **self-hosted OIDC provider** (`auth_providers: ["self-hosted"]`, `auth_flows: ["cookie","native_pkce"]`). What already exists on main covers the core flow: the probe (`probeRemoteAuthMode`) maps `auth_required: true` → OAuth mode regardless of provider, `deriveRemoteAuthProviderShape` renders "Sign in with <provider>" for any named provider, and the RFC 8252 native flow (`resolveLoginStrategy` → `runNativeLogin`) plus the embedded-webview fallback are provider-agnostic — the reporter's gateway advertises `native_pkce`, which the desktop supports since `7857d8737c`/`49423f8084`, with password-provider support extended in #75808 (merged Aug 14). If the reporter's gateway additionally sits behind an access proxy, this PR supplies the previously missing headers on every leg of that flow (provider preflight, authorize/token/refresh via `fetchJson`, ws-ticket, WS upgrade). Remaining gap (out of scope here, needs its own repro): the screenshot predates #75808 — "Remote gateway incomplete" with no button is the renderer treating the probe as unresolved, which on current main only happens when `/api/status` or `/api/auth/providers` is unreachable/unparseable from the desktop host. That is a diagnosis question (likely LAN reachability or an older backend), not a missing feature; if it reproduces on ≥ Aug-14 main, it should be a focused follow-up with the reporter's probe output. ## Validation - `npx vitest run electron/ src/app/settings/connections-settings.test.tsx src/lib/desktop-remote-auth.test.ts` — **98 files, 1226 passed, 2 skipped** - New tests written failing-first and sabotage-verified (reverting the probe header pass-through fails `gateway-ws-probe.test.ts`): registry header normalization/inheritance/dial-change/migration (5 tests), WS-probe header injection incl. the no-headers browser-safe path. - `npm run check:lint` (tsc `-p .`, `tsconfig.electron.json`, `tsconfig.e2e.json` + eslint) — exit 0. - `scripts/audit_pr_attribution.py --fix` — all contributor emails mapped (`tigercraft4` added). ## Infographic ![PR infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aa6a4c4/3irGpWnFwquzDh7_xFpEK_zGKBDE0H.png) --- Credit: core header-filtering/propagation design and implementation by @tigercraft4 in #74468 — cherry-picked with authorship preserved. This PR keeps #74468's history intact; the original PR can be closed as superseded by a maintainer once this merges.

signal.title: [Bug] Shift+Space still leaks raw CSI bytes into the buffer on main — follow-up to #86866
signal.text: Follow-up to #86866, which I'm unable to reopen (no permission) but which I believe wasn't actually fixed. Thanks for the quick turnaround on #87511/#87630 — the Ctrl+letter side works great. But Shift+Space is still broken on bab7be3 (main): the mapping from those PRs is on disk and the parser half works, yet the raw Shift+Space sequence still lands in the buffer. Repro (live install, prompt_toolkit 3.0.52, tmux over SSH, set -g escape-time 0): the script below installs the alias functions the same way cli.py:87-91 does, then feeds key sequences through a real Vt100Parser → Buffer: ``` python import asyncio, sys sys.path.insert(0, "/path/to/hermes-agent") # adjust from prompt_toolkit.buffer import Buffer from prompt_toolkit.layout import Layout, HSplit, Window, BufferControl from prompt_toolkit import Application from prompt_toolkit.input import create_pipe_input from hermes_cli import pt_input_extras as p p.install_shift_enter_alias(); p.install_ctrl_enter_alias() p.install_cmd_backspace_alias(); p.install_modify_other_keys_aliases() p.install_ignored_terminal_sequences() CASES = { "Ctrl+K xterm": "\x1b[27;5;107~", "Shift+Space xterm": "\x1b[27;2;32~", "Shift+Space kitty": "\x1b[32;2u", "plain space": " ", } async def probe(label, payload): buf = Buffer() with create_pipe_input() as inp: app = Application(layout=Layout(HSplit([Window(BufferControl(buf))])), input=inp) run_task = asyncio.ensure_future(app.run_async()) await asyncio.sleep(0.2) inp.send_text("ab") inp.send_text(payload) inp.send_text("cd") await asyncio.sleep(0.4) result = buf.text app.exit() try: await asyncio.wait_for(run_task, 2) except Exception: pass print(f"{label:22s} -> buffer={result!r}") async def main(): for label, payload in CASES.items(): await probe(label, payload) asyncio.run(main()) ``` Output on bab7be3: ``` Ctrl+K xterm -> buffer='abcd' Shift+Space xterm -> buffer='ab\x1b[27;2;32~cd' <-- leaks Shift+Space kitty -> buffer='ab\x1b[32;2ucd' <-- leaks plain space -> buffer='ab cd' ``` What I believe is happening: Vt100Parser._call_handler (vt100_parser.py:191) builds KeyPress(key, match.group(0)), so the KeyPress key is correctly mapped to ' ' by the new alias, but the data field still carries the full raw prefix. The character-insert binding (key_binding/bindings/basic.py:232) inserts event.data — the raw bytes — rather than the mapped key. For a normal space both fields are ' ' so it's invisible; for the extended sequence, data is the escape text and that's what gets inserted. (This is the pitfall the original issue mentioned: a bare " " mapping needs a handler that actually inserts the space.) Test note: test_shift_space_inserts_space asserts on key_press.key == ' ', which is parser output only — so it passes even though the buffer-level behavior leaks. A test that checks buffer contents after processing would catch this class of regression. A possible direction (either): 1. Map the token to a dedicated unused Keys member (e.g. Keys.ControlAt) plus one @kb.add handler that calls event.current_buffer.insert_text(' ') — sidesteps the data field, same pattern as the Ctrl/Alt bindings; or 2. Normalize the sequence to a bare space at parser level before KeyPress construction. Happy to help verify a fix. Thanks!

signal.title: fix(update): fall back to ZIP download when git fetch hits a trampoline
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Fixes the `git fetch` step in `hermes update` so it falls back to the ZIP download path on Windows when the `git` resolved from `PATH` is a broken Git-for-Windows trampoline launcher, instead of always exiting with a generic, unhelpful error. ## Related Issue Fixes #87876 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) ## Changes Made - `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py`: in `_cmd_update_impl`'s fetch-failure handling, detect the Git-for-Windows trampoline's distinctive `"BUG (fork bomb)"` stderr (issue #87876's root cause #1 — the small `bin\git.exe`/`cmd\git.exe` shim fails to re-exec the real `git-core` binary and refuses every git call instead of running it). This is a broken PATH entry, not a network/auth/filesystem problem, so it needs its own branch rather than falling into the generic "Failed to fetch updates from origin" exit. - On Windows, fall back to the ZIP download path — the same recovery every *other* git failure in this update flow already gets via the `CalledProcessError` handler further down (which never shells out to git). The initial fetch was the one exception: it reports its failure through a returncode rather than raising, so it never reached that handler. - On non-Windows (or if ZIP recovery isn't applicable), print an actionable message pointing at the broken PATH entry instead of the generic failure text. - `tests/hermes_cli/test_cmd_update.py`: new `TestFetchForkBombFallback` with two tests exercising `_cmd_update_impl` end-to-end (mocking `subprocess.run` to simulate the trampoline's fetch failure): - `test_falls_back_to_zip_on_windows` — confirms `_update_via_zip` is invoked and the update does not hard-exit. - `test_non_windows_exits_with_trampoline_message` — confirms the exit still happens off-Windows, but with the specific trampoline message rather than the generic "Failed to fetch updates from origin" text. Out of scope for this PR: the issue also describes venv-recreation atomicity and self-lock-during-replace failure modes. Both are already substantially covered by prior work in this codebase (the venv-holder detection/quarantine in `_detect_venv_python_processes`, `_abort_dependency_sync_if_self_locked`, and `_venv_core_imports_healthy` repair path, covered by `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_self_lock.py` and `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_venv_health.py`), so this PR is scoped to the one root cause (broken git trampoline) that had no handling at all. ## How to Test 1. `source .venv/bin/activate && python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_cmd_update.py -k ForkBomb -v` ``` tests/hermes_cli/test_cmd_update.py::TestFetchForkBombFallback::test_falls_back_to_zip_on_windows PASSED [ 50%] tests/hermes_cli/test_cmd_update.py::TestFetchForkBombFallback::test_non_windows_exits_with_trampoline_message PASSED [100%] 2 passed, 35 deselected in 0.67s ``` 2. signal.title: feat: surface unavailable config-gated tools at session start (refs #1433)
signal.text: ## Summary Implements **Phase 2** of #1433 (agent transparency): a one-time session-start notice listing **config-gated tools that are unavailable** — tools whose `check_fn` failed, so the model never sees them and the user never learns they exist. > ⓘ 5 tools unavailable (missing config/deps): browser_navigate, web_search, tts_speak, +2 more. Run `hermes tools` to configure. ## How it works - **`model_tools.py`** — extracted `_resolve_tool_names()` (the enabled-union/disabled-subtraction logic, behavior-identical) so the availability report shares the exact resolution used by `get_tool_definitions()`. New `get_unavailable_config_gated_tools()` computes requested − available and filters to `_CONFIG_GATED_TOOLSETS` (browser, vision, tts, web, image_gen, video_gen, x_search, homeassistant, spotify, discord, discord_admin). `check_fn` results are TTL-cached, so this costs no extra probes. - **`agent/agent_init.py`** — stores the list on the agent; the CLI prints the dim ⓘ line after the tools banner (non-quiet builds only). - **`tui_gateway/server.py`** — emits `tools.unavailable` (`{"names": [...]}`) once per session build (non-quiet). - **TUI** — new `tools.unavailable` event case; the notice renders as a dim event line after the intro, only on a fresh transcript. - **Desktop** — per-session store; the notice renders below the Intro in the fresh-session empty state. ## Design decisions - **Session start, not per-turn** — tool availability is static for the session; a per-turn segment would repeat the same static fact every turn and pollute the Phase 1 summary line's "what the agent did" contract. - **Curated whitelist** — only native toolsets whose unavailability is a config/setup gap are reported. Environment-gated tools (no browser binary, no Docker, worker mode), intentionally-disabled toolsets, and dynamic/MCP tools are never nagged about (`agent.disabled_toolsets` subtraction happens before the diff; MCP server tools are excluded by construction since their toolset is the server name). - **Cap 3 names + "+N more"**, with a pointer to `hermes tools` (the existing management surface) — no new UI. - No `check_fn` API change (bool-only, as today); a reason taxonomy ("API key missing" vs "binary missing") is deliberately out of scope. ## Verification - Python: 5 new unit tests (resolution sharing, whitelist filtering, disabled-toolset exclusion) + full `test_model_tools.py` / cache-isolation suites pass (33 tests). - TUI: 3 new event-handler tests (fresh-session surfacing, cap formatting, in-progress skip); full suite 1547 pass. - Desktop: 2 new wiring tests; full suite 3674 pass. - `tsc` + eslint clean in both apps. Refs #1433 — Phase 2 of a multi-phase plan (phases 1, 3, 4 tracked on the issue; related: #1092, #16636, #53007).

signal.title: [Bug]: Desktop Review pane "Create PR" always reports generic "is gh installed and authenticated?" even when gh is fine
signal.text: # Issue Draft: Desktop Review-pane "Create PR" button always reports `gh pr create failed (is gh installed and authenticated?)` — even when gh is installed, authenticated, and `gh auth status` is green **Status**: DRAFT — awaiting your review before `gh issue create`. Do NOT auto-post. **Target repo**: `NousResearch/hermes-agent` **Created by**: mugualucheshen (already authenticated via `gh auth status`) **Date**: 2026-08-16 **Local Hermes**: v0.20.1 (2026.8.13), upstream 7095e23e, local 5d526de2 (+1 carried commit) **Affected version**: Desktop `apps/desktop` v0.17.0, commit `56526bc0d3` ("Merge pull request #87630 from kshitijk4poor/fix/kitty-extended-keys-proper") — this is the commit that introduced the affected file. **Affected component**: Desktop (Electron app) → Review pane → ship-bar → PR button **Affected file**: `apps/desktop/electron/git-review-ops.ts`, function `reviewCreatePr()` at lines 765-779, and the helper `runGh()` at lines 35-44. --- ## Bug Description Clicking the PR icon button on the right-side audit panel of the Hermes Desktop app ("创建 PR" / "Create PR") fails with a misleading toast: > gh pr create failed (is gh installed and authenticated?) But `gh` IS installed and authenticated on the same machine. `gh auth status` reports a clean login with full `repo` scope. The toast is a generic fallback that hides the real failure. This is reproducible on macOS in any repo where the branch state doesn't satisfy `gh pr create --fill`'s expectations — e.g. when the upstream tracking branch is missing, when there's no commit ahead, when push hasn't completed yet, or when the local git binary resolution fails. Any non-zero exit from `gh pr create` triggers the same wrong message. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. `hermes update` to v0.20.1 (current `main`). 2. Launch the Hermes Desktop app. 3. Open any git repo (right sidebar → Review pane). 4. Make a commit ahead of the default branch on a local branch that does **not** yet have an upstream tracking ref set on the remote (e.g. a freshly cut branch). 5. Click the small PR-icon button on the right edge of the commit/ship bar. 6. Observe the toast: `gh pr create failed (is gh installed and authenticated?)`. 7. In the same shell, verify: `gh auth status` → green, `gh --version` → 2.86.0, `which gh` → `/opt/homebrew/bin/gh`. The error is a lie. A second reproducer: in a repo where the working branch is in a state that would normally cause `gh pr create` to print a useful stderr like `no commits between main and feature`, the toast is identical and the user is never told the real reason. ## Expected Behavior The error toast should surface `gh`'s real stderr so the user can act on it — for example: - `no commits between main and feature` - `aborted: you must first push the current branch` - `failed to run git: git: command not found` - `Your push would publish a private email address` If the failure is genuinely "gh not installed / not authenticated", the message should still be that — but only when that's actually what gh reported, not as a generic fallback for every error. A useful UX would mirror what the gh CLI itself does: show `gh`'s raw stderr tail in the toast, prefixed by which step failed (push vs create-vs-create). ## Actual Behavior A single fixed toast string regardless of root cause: > gh pr create failed (is gh installed and authenticated?) The user can't tell from the UI whether `gh` is missing, whether auth is broken, whether push failed, whether the branch has no commits, or whether the local git binary couldn't be resolved. They have to open a terminal and run `gh pr create` by hand to find out. ## Root Cause Analysis The bug lives in `apps/desktop/electron/git-review-ops.ts`. Two distinct defects combine to produce the wrong message. ### Defect 1: `runGh()` swallows stderr entirely Lines 35-44: ```typescript function runGh(args, cwd, ghBin): Promise<{ ok: boolean; stdout: string }> { return new Promise(resolve => { execFile( ghBin || 'gh', args, { cwd, env: ghEnv(ghBin), windowsHide: true, timeout: 30_000, maxBuffer: 8 * 1024 * 1024 }, (err, stdout) => resolve({ ok: !err, stdout: String(stdout || '') }) ) }) } ``` `execFile`'s callback receives `(err, stdout, stderr)`. This code destructures only `(err, stdout)` and discards stderr. By the time the caller throws, every useful error string (`gh`'s actual error message) is gone. ### Defect 2: `reviewCreatePr()` chains push + create with a swallowed push error, then attributes the failure to create Lines 765-779: ```typescript async function reviewCreatePr(repoPath, gitBin, ghBin) { const cwd = resolveRequestedPathForIpc(repoPath, { purpose: 'Review create PR' }) await reviewPush(repoPath, gitBin).catch(() => undefined) // ← push failure swallowed const created = await runGh(['pr', 'create', '--fill'], cwd, ghBin) if (!created.ok) { throw new Error('gh pr create failed (is gh installed and authenticated?)') // ← static message } ... } ``` Two issues: 1. `reviewPush(...)` failures are silently caught (`.catch(() => undefined)`). When push fails — the most common real-world reason a subsequent `gh pr create` will fail — the cause is lost. The function proceeds to `gh pr create`, which then fails for a derived reason, and the toast still says "gh pr create failed". 2. The thrown `Error` is a hard-coded string with no stderr attached. Even if `runGh` returned stderr, this throw drops it. ### Note on the surrounding infrastructure For context, the file does have some prior art for handling this correctly: - `resolveGhBinary()` (main.ts:2406) — caches a resolved path with a Homebrew/PATH fallback (added because GUI-launched Electron apps inherit a minimal PATH). So `ghBin` itself is generally correct; `gh` is being invoked. The toast text was written as if `gh` weren't there at all. - `ghEnv()` (git-review-ops.ts:25) — also explicitly augments PATH for the same reason. Both pieces of infrastructure say "we know GUI apps have a minimal PATH, we compensate"; the error toast text doesn't reflect this. ## Proposed Fix A minimal change that preserves the public API and fixes the message. Suggested patch: ```diff -function runGh(args, cwd, ghBin): Promise<{ ok: boolean; stdout: string }> { - return new Promise(resolve => { - execFile( - ghBin || 'gh', - args, - { cwd, env: ghEnv(ghBin), windowsHide: true, timeout: 30_000, maxBuffer: 8 * 1024 * 1024 }, - (err, stdout) => resolve({ ok: !err, stdout: String(stdout || '') }) - ) - }) -} +function runGh(args, cwd, ghBin): Promise<{ ok: boolean; stdout: string; stderr: string; code: number | null }> { + return new Promise(resolve => { + execFile( + ghBin || 'gh', + args, + { cwd, env: ghEnv(ghBin), windowsHide: true, timeout: 30_000, maxBuffer: 8 * 1024 * 1024 }, + (err, stdout, stderr) => + resolve({ + ok: !err, + stdout: String(stdout || ''), + stderr: String(stderr || ''), + code: err && typeof err.code === 'number' ? err.code : null, + }) + ) + }) +} async function reviewCreatePr(repoPath, gitBin, ghBin) { const cwd = resolveRequestedPathForIpc(repoPath, { purpose: 'Review create PR' }) - await reviewPush(repoPath, gitBin).catch(() => undefined) + // Surface push errors distinctly so the user can fix the push before retrying, + // instead of having the toast blame `gh pr create`. + try { + await reviewPush(repoPath, gitBin) + } catch (pushErr) { + const pushMsg = pushErr instanceof Error ? pushErr.message : String(pushErr || 'push failed') + throw new Error(`Push failed: ${pushMsg}`) + } const created = await runGh(['pr', 'create', '--fill'], cwd, ghBin) if (!created.ok) { - throw new Error('gh pr create failed (is gh installed and authenticated?)') + const tail = (created.stderr || '').trim().split('\n').filter(Boolean).slice(-3).join(' · ') || '(no stderr)' + throw new Error(`gh pr create failed: ${tail}`) } const url = created.stdout.trim().split('\n').filter(Boolean).pop() || '' return { url } } ``` Also update any other `runGh` call sites in the same file (`reviewShipInfo`, `reviewFetchPrComment`, `reviewPrList`) to consume `stderr` if they currently swallow it. A `git grep -n "runGh(" apps/desktop/electron/git-review-ops.ts` confirms five call sites. A defensive belt-and-braces improvement: have `resolveGhBinary()` also verify the resolved path with `fs.accessSync(p, fs.constants.X_OK)` so the toast can say "gh binary at /opt/homebrew/bin/gh is not executable" when that's the real reason, instead of misleadingly asking the user to install gh. ## Operating System macOS 26.4.1 (Apple Silicon, `/opt/homebrew/bin/gh`) ## Hermes Version ``` $ hermes version Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (2026.8.13) · upstream 7095e23e · local 5d526de2 (+1 carried commit) ``` ## Debug Report Local reproduction only; no remote debug paste needed because the bug is fully characterized from source. The affected file is committed at `56526bc0d3` on `main` and was last touched by commit `39d09453f9` ("feat(desktop): ts-ify everything", ethernet8023, 2026-06-29) which created the file. For developers wanting to reproduce locally without the GUI, the equivalent shell command is: ```bash gh pr create --fill --repo <owner>/<repo> ``` in a branch state that gh rejects. The Desktop app's `runGh` wrapper around this same call discards stderr and throws a hard-coded message — so the bug is independent of whether the user can run `gh pr create` from their terminal. ## Additional Logs / Traceback The Desktop app does not log `runGh`'s stderr to the main process log either; nothing currently surfaces it. A useful follow-up would be `console.error('[gh]', created.stderr)` in the catch path before re-throwing, so the Electron main log captures the real reason for users who are debugging via logs. ## Proposed Fix See "Proposed Fix" section above. Ready to submit as a PR if maintainers agree the API change to `runGh` (adding `stderr` and `code` to its return shape) is acceptable. The change is backwards compatible because `runGh` is file-local. --- ## Labels (suggested) - `bug` - `area/desktop` - `comp/review-pane` ## Willingness to submit a PR - [x] Yes — happy to submit a PR with the proposed patch, scoped to `git-review-ops.ts` only. - [ ] No --- ## Pre-flight checklist before posting - [ ] Re-confirm issue title (currently `[Bug]: Desktop Review pane "Create PR" always reports generic "is gh installed and authenticated?" even when gh is fine`) - [ ] Re-confirm labels (`bug` / `area/desktop` / `comp/review-pane` — adjust if the repo's label set differs) - [ ] Run `gh issue create --repo NousResearch/hermes-agent --title "..." --body-file <this.md> --label bug --label area/desktop --label comp/review-pane` - [ ] Confirm URL lands and copy into issue log

signal.title: fix(langfuse): close failed api traces
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Failed provider requests can currently be visible in Hermes logs while missing from Langfuse as usable failed traces. The reproduced case is a custom DeepSeek-compatible provider returning HTTP 402 before any streamed response is delivered: `pre_api_request` starts the Langfuse trace/generation, `api_request_error` records the failed attempt, but the terminal billing/error branch returns directly from `agent/conversation_loop.py` and never reaches the normal `agent/turn_finalizer.py` `on_session_end` emission. This PR makes failed provider calls visible as errored Langfuse generations and ensures terminal API-error returns close the turn trace. The success-path trace flow and existing generation fields are preserved. Related open PRs: #81874 and #81732 cover adjacent Langfuse failure-marking work. This PR includes the request-error hook wiring needed on current `main` and adds the core-loop lifecycle fix for terminal provider exceptions that skip `finalize_turn`. ## Related Issue Related to #81731 and the Langfuse failed-observation reports in #81874 / #81732. ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) ## Changes Made - `plugins/observability/langfuse/__init__.py` - Add `api_request_error` handling for failed provider calls. - End the matching generation with `level="ERROR"` and a redacted `status_message`. - Include failure metadata: status code, retry counts, retryability, classifier reason, duration, error type, and safe summary. - Flush immediately after ending a failed generation. - `plugins/observability/langfuse/plugin.yaml` - Declare the `api_request_error` hook. - `agent/conversation_loop.py` - Emit `on_session_end` before direct terminal API-error returns so Langfuse can close the root turn trace even when `finalize_turn` is skipped. - `tests/plugins/test_langfuse_plugin.py` - Add hook registration/no-op coverage and regression coverage for failed generations. - `tests/run_agent/test_run_agent.py` - Add a DeepSeek-style HTTP 402 billing regression test asserting `api_request_error` and `on_session_end` share the same `api_request_id`. ## How to Test 1. Automated checks run locally: - `python3 -m pytest tests/plugins/test_langfuse_plugin.py tests/run_agent/test_run_agent.py::TestRunConversation::test_terminal_api_error_emits_session_end_hook tests/run_agent/test_31273_402_not_retried.py` - Result: `31 passed` - `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD` 2. Manual repro path: - Enable `observability/langfuse` with valid Langfuse credentials. - Configure a custom DeepSeek-compatible provider with a key/account that returns HTTP 402. - Send a chat turn. Expected: Hermes still returns the billing error to the caller, and Langfuse receives an errored generation plus a closed root turn trace for that failed request. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS, Python 3.13.9 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — N/A - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — N/A, pure Python lifecycle/plugin logic - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A ## Screenshots / Logs Representative failing local log before the core-loop lifecycle fix: ```text Langfuse tracing: started trace ... for task:...:turn:...:api... Streaming failed before delivery: Error code: 402 - Insufficient Balance API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=APIStatusError provider=custom base_url=https://api.deepseek.com model=deepseek-v4-flash summary=HTTP 402: Insufficient Balance Non-retryable client error: Error code: 402 - ... ```

signal.title: fix(desktop): surface real gh stderr in Review pane PR create errors
signal.text: Fixes #87731. The Review pane's Create-PR button always reported the generic `gh pr create failed (is gh installed and authenticated?)` toast even when gh was installed and authenticated, because `runGh` discarded stderr and `reviewCreatePr` mapped every non-zero exit to that one message. Changes: - `runGh` now captures stderr (from both the error object and the callback's stderr arg) and returns it alongside `ok`/`stdout`. - `reviewCreatePr` throws `gh pr create failed: <real stderr>` when gh exits non-zero, falling back to the generic message only when stderr is empty. The renderer's existing `notifyError` path surfaces the thrown message, so users now see the actual reason (e.g. `no commits between main and feature`) instead of a lie. Tests: - `reviewCreatePr` surfaces gh stderr on failure. - `reviewCreatePr` falls back to the generic message when stderr is empty. Verified: electron vitest suite passes, `tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json --noEmit` clean, eslint + prettier clean on touched files.

signal.title: fix(cli): honour model_aliases api_key, stop cross-provider key leak (#83612)
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? A `model_aliases:` entry that points at a custom endpoint could not authenticate, and leaked a credential doing it. Two compounding causes, exactly as reported in #83612: 1. **The alias's key was never read.** `DirectAlias` carried only `(model, provider, base_url)`, so `_load_direct_aliases()` silently discarded any `api_key` in the config entry. 2. **The wrong key was sent instead.** `switch_model()` resolves credentials against the *default* provider, and only afterwards overwrites `base_url` with the alias endpoint — keeping the key it had already resolved. So switching to the alias 401s, and the default provider's secret goes out to an unrelated third-party host (including on the `/v1/models` validation probe). `hermes chat -m <alias>` had the matching half: `oneshot` passed the alias's `base_url` to `resolve_runtime_provider()` but not its key, so a custom host whose vendor key isn't derivable from the hostname never authenticated. **Why this approach:** rather than add a second credential-selection path, the alias override now re-resolves through `resolve_runtime_provider(explicit_base_url=...)`. That branch already honours an explicit key first and host-gates env-key fallbacks (#28660), so the hardened logic is reused rather than duplicated. The pre-alias key is kept only when the alias resolves to the **same host** it was resolved for — which is what keeps users pinned to a custom endpoint working — and dropped otherwise. Because the drop is keyed on host mismatch rather than on which branch produced the key, sessions on **built-in** providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, …) are covered too, not just custom ones. ## Related Issue Fixes #83612 Related prior work, neither of which is in `main` (`DirectAlias` still carries only `(model, provider, base_url)`): - #71410 — open, fixes the leak for the custom-provider branch. Its last review round flagged that built-in/registered-API-key providers still leak with direct aliases; the host-mismatch rule here covers that case, with tests. Happy to fold this into that PR instead if the author prefers. - #66409 — proposed the same `DirectAlias` `api_key`/`key_env` fields, closed by its author (#66437 was closed as its duplicate). ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [x] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `hermes_cli/model_switch.py` - `DirectAlias` gains `api_key` / `key_env`, both defaulted — existing positional construction `DirectAlias(model, provider, base_url)` is unchanged. - `_load_direct_aliases()` reads both from `model_aliases:` entries. - New `direct_alias_api_key()` resolves a literal key, a `"${VAR}"` reference, or `key_env`. Env reads go through `_scoped_key_env` so a multiplexed gateway can't hand one profile another profile's key. - The direct-alias override re-resolves credentials against the alias endpoint, and reuses the pre-alias key only on a host match. The resolver's `no-key-required` placeholder is normalised so a same-host credential still outranks it. When the alias declares its own key the resolver is skipped entirely, avoiding a second local-endpoint model probe. - `hermes_cli/oneshot.py` — passes the alias's key as `explicit_api_key` alongside the existing `explicit_base_url`. - `hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py` — the direct-alias branch of `_resolve_named_custom_runtime()` gains the `OLLAMA_API_KEY` host gate it was missing. `_host_derived_api_key()` documents that it deliberately skips `OLLAMA_API_KEY` because an explicit host-matched path handles it (GHSA-76xc-57q6-vm5m); that path existed for named custom providers but not for direct aliases, so an Ollama Cloud alias resolved no key at all once routed through it. - `tests/hermes_cli/test_model_alias_credentials_83612.py` — new, 19 cases. - Docs for the new keys: `cli-config.yaml.example`, `website/docs/user-guide/configuring-models.md`, `website/docs/reference/slash-commands.md`, and the agent-facing `skills/autonomous-ai-agents/hermes-agent/references/providers-and-models.md`. ## How to Test Reproduce the bug on `main`: 1. Set a credentialed default provider, e.g. `OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-...` with `model.provider: openrouter`. 2. Add an alias pointing somewhere else, with its own key: ```yaml model_aliases: theta: model: theta-1 provider: custom base_url: "https://theta.example.com/v1" api_key: "sk-theta-..." ``` 3. Run `/model theta` (or `hermes chat -m theta`). On `main` the request carries `sk-or-...` to `theta.example.com` — 401, and the OpenRouter key has left the building. With this PR it carries `sk-theta-...`. The leak cases assert on the credential handed to the endpoint probe — what actually goes on the wire — not just on the returned struct. Credential selection stays host-**matched**, not substring-matched, and there are tests for that: `ollama.com.attacker.test` and `127.0.0.1/ollama.com/v1` get no credential. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate — see **Related Issue** above; signal.title: fix(config): parse YAML list/dict values in set_config_value
signal.text: ## Problem `hermes config set custom_providers '- name: oneapi\n type: openai...'` writes the value as a quoted string, not a YAML array. The config file ends up with `custom_providers: '[{"name":"oneapi",...}]'` (string) instead of proper YAML list structure. Hermes then fails to parse custom_providers as a list. ## Root cause `set_config_value` in `hermes_cli/config.py` receives its `value` as a `str` from argparse. The existing coercion block (lines 5284-5295) only handles bool/int/float — no YAML parse attempt. Multi-line YAML input stays as a raw string and gets written verbatim to config.yaml. ## Fix After the existing bool/int/float coercion, add a YAML parse fallback: - If the value contains a newline or starts with `-`, `{`, or `[` (YAML collection indicators), attempt `yaml.safe_load(value)`. - If it succeeds and returns a non-str type (list, dict, etc.), use the parsed value. - If it fails (YAMLError) or returns a str, keep the original coerced value. - Scalars already coerced to bool/int/float above are unaffected — the `isinstance(value, str)` guard skips them. `yaml` is already imported at the top of `config.py` (line 330), so no new import needed. ## Tests New file `tests/hermes_cli/test_config_set_yaml.py` (16 tests): 1. **Bug-injection proof** — multi-line YAML list stored as `list` (not `str`). Verified: removing the fix → 4 tests FAIL; restoring → all pass. 2. **Scalar regression** — bool/int/float/str/enum coercion unchanged (6 bool params + int + float + plain string + string-typed enum). 3. **Single-line dict** — `{enabled: true, name: test}` parses to dict. 4. **Single-line list** — `[alpha, beta, gamma]` parses to list. 5. **Invalid YAML fallback** — value with newline that parses back to str stays str; malformed YAML (`{a: 1`) raises YAMLError and keeps original string. All 99 tests pass (16 new + 83 existing `test_set_config_value.py`).

signal.title: fix(skills): treat a package-root external dir as its own skill name
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Fixes `/<skill>` slash invocation for the layout where a `skills.external_dirs` entry **is the skill package itself** (a one-skill repo configured as its own directory, containing `SKILL.md`) rather than a parent of many skills. `normalize_skill_lookup_name()` assumed every external dir is a parent root, so `relative_to(root)` produced `"."` — not a `skill_view()`-safe name. `_load_skill_payload()` then returned `None` and slash dispatch fell through with the misleading `not a quick/plugin/bundle/skill command: wayfinder`, even though discovery had registered the skill and the `/` picker advertised it (#88064). When the relative path is `"."`, the normalizer now returns the package directory name — the identifier discovery registered the skill under. Parent-dir layouts and `~/.hermes/skills/<name>` are unchanged. ## Related Issue Fixes #88064 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) ## Changes Made - `agent/skill_utils.py` — `normalize_skill_lookup_name()`: the trusted-root loop keeps a `relative_to` that yields `"."` from falling through as a bare dot; it returns `identifier_path.name` instead, with a comment documenting the one-skill-package layout. - `tests/agent/test_skill_utils.py` — `TestNormalizeSkillLookupName` gains the package-root regression: external dir == skill package normalizes to the package name, never `"."`. ## How to Test 1. `python -m pytest tests/agent/test_skill_utils.py -q` 2. Observed result: 24 passed. A/B guard: with only the `agent/skill_utils.py` hunk stashed, the new test FAILS (the normalizer returns `"."`), with the hunk it passes. 3. `python -m pytest tests/agent/test_skill_commands.py -q` — Observed result: 25 passed (the dispatch-side payload loader consumers are unaffected). 4. Manual repro from the issue: with `skills.external_dirs: [/path/to/my-skills/wayfinder]`, `/wayfinder` now resolves through `skill_view("wayfinder")` instead of erroring; a parent-dir entry keeps its nested relative form. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [x] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 15 (arm64) ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A - [ ] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A - [ ] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A - [ ] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A ## Screenshots / Logs ``` $ pytest tests/agent/test_skill_utils.py -q # with fix 24 passed in 0.47s $ git stash -- agent/skill_utils.py && pytest ... -q # A/B guard 1 failed (normalize returned "." for the package-root layout) ```

signal.title: fix(desktop): preserve pre-tool assistant text
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes disappearing assistant text in Desktop tool-using turns through two complementary paths: - preserve provider-neutral text that appeared before the last tool boundary when `message.complete` settles the trailing final segment; - project explicit OpenAI Codex `phase=commentary` sidecar text into a client-only `display_content` field for session hydration, without mutating canonical assistant content or replay state. ## Root cause For ordinary providers, Desktop completion reconciliation removed every streamed text part before appending the final response. For Codex Responses, public pre-tool commentary can be persisted in `codex_message_items` while canonical `content` remains empty; the sessions API omitted that sidecar entirely, so reload could not reconstruct text that had been visible live. Related visible symptom: #53204. This PR also covers the Codex empty-canonical-content hydration variant that a renderer-only fix cannot recover. ## Safety and privacy - projects only `type=message`, `phase=commentary`, `type=output_text` parts; - never exposes raw `codex_message_items`; - never promotes `phase=analysis`; - honors `display.show_commentary=false` on GET-session and `run.completed` projections; - forces secret and URL-credential redaction at the API egress boundary; - leaves canonical assistant content, role ordering, tool pairing, prompt caching, and Codex continuation replay unchanged. ## Tests - `201 passed` across the focused 11-file API-server suite; - `130 passed` across API session/run tests after the final read-only config-loader refinement; - `85 passed` across Desktop message/interim suites; - Desktop TypeScript typecheck passed; - Desktop production build and `assert-dist-built` passed; - four unrelated full-suite timeout failures rerun in isolation: `20 passed`; - independent fail-closed security/correctness review passed with no concerns or logic errors. ## Notes The full Windows gateway suite is not used as a completion claim: it exceeded the 10-minute local ceiling with unrelated platform failures. The focused API-server surface changed here completed cleanly.

signal.title: fix(desktop): self-heal dropped SSH/HTTP remote connections + status bar reconnect (#82679, #80430)
signal.text: ## Summary Hermes Desktop now **self-heals a dropped SSH/HTTP registered remote connection** — automatic bounded-backoff boot retries with a manual status-bar Reconnect action — instead of parking on "Desktop boot failed" until the user deletes and re-enters the exact same connection details. Salvages open contributor PR #80694 by @fangliquanflq (status-bar reconnect, cherry-picked with authorship preserved) and builds the self-heal class fix for the primary/registered-connection path on top. Fixes #82679 Fixes #80430 ## Root cause The remote-connection lifecycle already handled the *post-boot* drop (renderer reconnect loop with full-jitter backoff + `revalidateConnection` cache invalidation), and secondaries already had their own backoff loop in `store/gateway.ts`. The uncovered class was the **failed boot of a registered primary remote**: 1. A dropped SSH/HTTP transport surfaces at the next boot as a transient transport error (`"Could not verify the existing SSH backend"`, `ERR_CONNECTION_RESET`, mint timeout). `shouldLatchBackendStartFailure` correctly does **not** latch it — but nothing ever **re-attempted** the boot: the renderer's reconnect machinery only arms after `bootCompleted`. The app sat on the terminal failure overlay; manual re-entry "fixed" it only because it forced the fresh bootstrap an automatic retry would have performed. 2. On the SSH leg, a reused cached master whose lifecycle probe failed was **kept** in `sshConnections`, so every subsequent attempt re-failed through the same wedged master/tunnel until re-entered details changed the config fingerprint and forced a teardown. ## Changes **Commit 1 — salvaged from #80694 (author @fangliquanflq):** - `store/gateway-reconnect.ts` — single-flight renderer reconnect action, registered by `use-gateway-boot`'s existing profile-aware reconnect path - `app/shell/gateway-menu-panel.tsx` — Reconnect button in the gateway status menu whenever the socket is not open (re-applied here; the PR's pill-plugin file moved on main) - Localized copy for en/ar/ja/zh/zh-hant + behavior tests **Commit 2 — self-heal class fix:** - `electron/backend-start-failure.ts` — new `isRetryableRemoteBootFailure()`: remote + non-reauth ⇒ transient/retryable; local failures and confirmed 401/403 are not (*a missing capability differs from a transient failure*) - `electron/main.ts` — boot-failure broadcast now carries `retryable` (rides with `error` through `updateBootProgress`); failed SSH reuse probe tears down the stale cached master so the next attempt bootstraps fresh - `use-gateway-boot.ts` — bounded self-heal loop: up to **5** boot re-attempts with the same full-jitter backoff shape as the socket reconnect loop (2s base, 15s cap); exhausted retries end in the real boot-failure recovery overlay — never an infinite spinner; reset on success/soft-switch, timer cleared on unmount - `store/boot.ts` — `resumeDesktopBootForRetry()` re-arms the overlay with retry status while an automatic retry is in flight ## Validation | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | `vitest` electron/backend-start-failure.test.ts (predicate matrix, retryable vs reauth-latch exclusivity) | ✅ pass | | `vitest` use-gateway-boot.test.tsx (13 tests: transient SSH failure self-heals on retry; retries bounded at 6 total dials then recovery overlay, no further attempts; non-retryable fails immediately) | ✅ pass | | `vitest` gateway-reconnect.test.ts + gateway-menu-panel.test.tsx (salvaged) | ✅ pass | | Sabotage verification (disable retry budget / predicate) | ✅ 4 tests fail as expected, restored green | | `tsc -p tsconfig.json` / `tsconfig.electron.json` / `tsconfig.e2e.json` | ✅ clean | | `eslint` on all touched files | ✅ clean | | `scripts/audit_pr_attribution.py --fix` | ✅ all contributor emails mapped | One salvaged test assertion was updated to current main's contract (primary reconnect dials the window-owned backend with no profile arg — post-#46651 semantics). ## #58875 (React stack overflow on remote gateway connect) Investigated separately and **out of scope for this PR**: per @DavidMetcalfe's analysis on the issue, it is a renderer-side `@assistant-ui/react` infinite render loop inside `AssistantMessage` *after* a successful connection — a different layer from the connection lifecycle touched here. The reporter reinstalled and can no longer reproduce, and no repro currently exists to write a failing test against, so claiming a fix would be dishonest. Referenced here for the cluster record only; it remains open. ## Infographic ![Desktop remote reconnect self-heal](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aa6a494/5E6u7SrIGULZu64MVfGkn_TOI6yNgR.png) --- Credit to @fangliquanflq for the status-bar reconnect groundwork (#80694), preserved as an authored commit on this branch.

signal.title: [Bug]: Windows update frequently fails / partial updates block runtime repair (broken Git trampolines + venv python.exe missing + self-lock)
signal.text: ### Bug Description Title: Windows update frequently fails / partial updates block runtime repair (broken Git trampolines + venv python.exe missing + self-lock) Labels: bug, Windows, update, installer, high-priority Body: Summary On Windows, hermes update often stalls or only partially completes and requires manual recovery. Root causes are three interacting platform issues: Hermes-bundled and system Git installs can be 46KB trampoline launchers that fail with "BUG (fork bomb)" and do not re-exec git-core correctly. A partial update/venv recreate can leave the venv without a console interpreter (venv\Scripts\python.exe), leaving only pythonw.exe. That breaks uv-style trampolines (error: "uv trampoline failed to canonicalize script path"). Running the update from hermes.exe (or the venv python) self-locks the launcher/venv files, preventing the update from quarantining/replacing runtime files (e.g., managed Python runtime and SQLite), so the final runtime repair step fails. Observed behavior Update fetch may succeed (or partially succeed via ZIP fallback) but the final quarantine/replace step fails with a file lock because hermes.exe (the running process that launched the update) still holds the executable and/or venv python open. git --version returns "BUG (fork bomb)" (46KB trampoline output) because PATH resolves to broken trampolines (bin\git.exe or cmd\git.exe). The real git binary exists at mingw64\libexec\git-core\git.exe (≈4.4 MB) and works when invoked directly. After a failed/partial update, venv still contains site-packages but no python.exe, so uv-trampoline launchers fail to run Hermes. Manual recovery required: prepend mingw64\libexec\git-core to PATH and set GIT_EXEC_PATH to that dir (session-only), and re-run the update driven by SYSTEM Python (not hermes.exe). Example that repaired my installation: $env:GIT_EXEC_PATH="C:\Program Files\Git\mingw64\libexec\git-core" 𝑒 𝑛 𝑣 : 𝑃 𝐴 𝑇 𝐻 = " 𝐶 : \Program 𝐹 𝑖 𝑙 𝑒 𝑠 \Git \mingw 64 \libexec \git − 𝑐 𝑜 𝑟 𝑒 ; " + env:PATH="C:\ProgramFiles\Git\mingw64\libexec\git−core;"+env:PATH & "C:\Users<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python313\python.exe" -c "import sys; sys.argv=['hermes','update']; from hermes_cli.main import main; main()" After doing the above, update completed, venv recreated, dependencies reinstalled, and managed Python runtime updated (SQLite fixed). Why this is critical Non-technical users will be left with broken installs or will need lengthy support sessions. Partial update that cannot replace runtime leaves Hermes in an inconsistent state (old vulnerable SQLite still present until manual fix). The problem is reproducible on Windows when trampolines are present and when updates attempt runtime replacement while the launcher is running. Reproduction checklist On Windows, install Hermes (bundled PortableGit in AppData\Local\hermes\git). Ensure bin\git.exe and cmd\git.exe trampolines exist but their reexec target is broken or not found (or simulate by altering PATH so trampolines resolve first while git-core is intact). Run hermes update normally via hermes.exe. Observe: git calls fail ("BUG (fork bomb)") or are intercepted by trampoline guard. Update may proceed through ZIP fallback but fails when attempting to quarantine/replace hermes.exe (file lock). Verify venv\Scripts\python.exe may be absent if a venv recreation occurred in the partially-applied update. Fix by running update from a system Python process with GIT_EXEC_PATH and PATH pointed at mingw64\libexec\git-core — observe success. Exact environment & artifacts (from my run) Hermes agent path: C:\Users\Seth\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent System Python: 3.13.15 (C:\Users\Seth\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python313) Broken trampoline size: ~46 KB (bin\git.exe, cmd\git.exe) Real git-core binary: C:\Program Files\Git\mingw64\libexec\git-core\git.exe (≈4.38 MB), works when called directly Errors observed: "uv trampoline failed to canonicalize script path" "BUG (fork bomb)" Update blocked due to file lock when attempting to quarantine/replace hermes.exe Root-cause diagnosis (concise) The launcher/trampoline model (small launcher that reexecs a larger git-core) is brittle if PATH/env are altered or helper files are missing; trampolines emit a fork-bomb guard and fail. The update flow runs destructive steps (quarantine/replace managed runtime) from inside the running launcher process (hermes.exe), which causes file locks on Windows and prevents atomic replacement. Venv recreation isn't atomic and can leave an incomplete venv with site-packages but missing python.exe, breaking launchers that expect console interpreter to exist. Recommended fixes (prioritized) High priority (reduce support pain immediately) Change the update flow to avoid performing runtime replacement/quarantine steps from inside the running launcher. On Windows, spawn an external system-python helper (or a short-lived installer process) that performs the replace/rename operations so hermes.exe and venv\Scripts\python.exe are not held open during replacement. Add an explicit pre-update healthcheck and fail-fast with clear troubleshooting guidance: Confirm git --version returns a valid version; if it appears to be a trampoline, probe mingw64\libexec\git-core\git.exe and prefer that in-session for the update. Confirm venv\Scripts\python.exe exists. If missing, either recreate the venv in an atomic safe way or require update to be run via system Python automatically. Provide a documented --use-system-python (or --no-self-lock) flag that triggers the system-Python-driven update sequence automatically. Medium priority (robustness) Provide a user config option (e.g. hermes.git_path) to point the updater at a specific git binary if the PATH-resolved git is unreliable. Make the venv recreate process atomic — create a new venv directory then replace/rename it into place only after it is fully populated, to avoid leaving a half-recreated venv. Improve the ZIP fallback/update logic to prefer using real git-core when present, rather than relying on PATH-resolved bare git. Low priority / ergonomics When quarantine/replace fails due to file lock, print a clear actionable message: e.g., "Update partially applied. To finish runtime repair, re-run this update from system Python: ." Offer a --finish-update helper that runs the system-Python-driven remainder. Add logging/telemetry that distinguishes "partial update applied, quarantine failed due to file lock" so support can triage quickly. Consider shipping a small robust shim for PortableGit that correctly sets GIT_EXEC_PATH for its subprocesses and is tolerant to PATH manipulations. Suggested minimal fix patch (developer guidance) Implement update orchestration like: Pre-flight: detect if runtime replacement is required. If yes: launch a system-Python helper process (or elevated updater) that: Terminates/ensures no hermes.exe or venv python processes are running Performs the replace/quarantine atomically Restarts the user agent if appropriate Alternatively, provide hermes update --use-system-python which does the above. Attachments / logs to help debugging Sample transcript with the exact commands that worked for me: $env:GIT_EXEC_PATH="C:\Program Files\Git\mingw64\libexec\git-core" 𝑒 𝑛 𝑣 : 𝑃 𝐴 𝑇 𝐻 = " 𝐶 : \Program 𝐹 𝑖 𝑙 𝑒 𝑠 \Git \mingw 64 \libexec \git − 𝑐 𝑜 𝑟 𝑒 ; " + env:PATH="C:\ProgramFiles\Git\mingw64\libexec\git−core;"+env:PATH & "C:\Users<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python313\python.exe" -c "import sys; sys.argv=['hermes','update']; from hermes_cli.main import main; main()" Sizes and paths for trampolines vs real binaries (46KB vs 4.4MB) Observed hermes doctor outputs before/after showing SQLite moved from 3.50.4 → 3.53.1 after the system-Python-driven update Request Please confirm whether you can: Add a documented system-Python-driven update path or auto-fallback when runtime replacement is required. Add pre-update health checks for PATH/git and venv python presence. Provide a supported configuration option to pin the git binary used by the updater. I can provide full logs, transcripts, and help test a patch or pre-release fix. Thank you — resolving these issues will greatly reduce Windows support burden and make updates reliable for end users. (If helpful, I can also paste a 3–4 line “how to recover” snippet for docs or a one-paragraph summary for the issue title.) ### Steps to Reproduce in the body ### Expected Behavior This has happened to me after every update of the windows hermes app ### Actual Behavior takes a ton of time to fix ### Affected Component Setup / Installation ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) N/A (CLI only) ### Debug Report ```shell s ``` ### Operating System windows 11 pro ### Python Version _No response_ ### Hermes Version _No response_ ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) _No response_ ### Proposed Fix (optional) _No response_ ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

signal.title: feat(tts): local MLX Qwen3-TTS streaming provider (qwen3tts-mlx)
signal.text: ## Summary Adds a **local MLX streaming TTS provider** (`qwen3tts-mlx`) so Hermes conversational voice (session speech, voice bubbles) can run on a local Qwen3-TTS voice-clone engine over Apple's MLX GPU path — no cloud dependency, custom voice clone support, ~4-9s TTFB per sentence instead of waiting ~47s for a whole buffer. ## Background Hermes already has a `StreamingTTSProvider` ABC (`tools/tts_streaming.py`) with cloud streamers (elevenlabs/openai/gemini/xai). Local TTS engines are supported for **synchronous** synthesis via command providers (`tts.providers.<name>.type: command`) — and users on Apple Silicon have been running exactly that (see `skills/productivity/local-tts-optimization`, PR #85041). But conversational voice falls back to per-sentence sync synthesis, which for a local engine means each sentence pays full model-load + whole-buffer latency. mlx-audio's Qwen3-TTS generator **is** a generator: with newline-separated input it yields audio per segment as soon as each finishes. Measured on M5 Max: 4 segments stream at t=4.2s/7.6s/11.6s/16.9s vs 47s for one whole-buffer call. This PR wires that capability into the existing streaming pipeline. ## Design - `@register("qwen3tts-mlx")` in `tools/tts_streaming.py`; class implements `available()` (MLX venv + worker script exist) and `stream(text)` - `stream()` spawns a dedicated **MLX venv subprocess** (`~/.hermes/tts/mlx_stream_worker.py`) and reads back frames of `[u32 length][int16 PCM]`. The worker splits text on newlines, synthesizes each segment via `model.generate(..., ref_audio, ref_text, lang_code="Chinese")`, and writes each PCM frame immediately. - **Subprocess isolation is mandatory**: mlx-audio pins `transformers 5.0.0rc3`, which conflicts with `qwen_tts`'s pinned `4.57.3` in the Hermes runtime venv (`check_model_inputs() missing 'func'`). Keeping MLX in its own venv and bridging via subprocess follows the same pattern as command providers. - Config surface is additive: `tts.streaming.provider: qwen3tts-mlx` selects it; `tts.streaming.qwen3tts-mlx.model_dir` / `.ref_audio` override defaults. ## Verification - `python -m pytest tests/tools/test_tts_streaming_mlx.py -x -q` → 6 passed (registry membership, availability, frame ordering, worker-failure propagation, section-based args) - Full streaming + chunking suite: 39 passed, 12 skipped - Live E2E on this machine: `Qwen3TTSMLXStreamer.stream("…\n…")` yielded 3 PCM frames (TTFB 8.8s incl. model load), correct 24kHz int16 layout ## Who should enable this - Apple Silicon users who run a local Qwen3-TTS voice-clone engine and want **conversational voice** (not just on-demand synthesis) with a custom cloned voice, no cloud cost, private by design - Anyone who already has the `local-tts-optimization` setup (PR #85041) and wants streaming voice on top ## Platform compatibility | Platform | Impact | |---|---| | macOS Apple Silicon | ✅ Primary (MLX + mlx-audio) | | macOS Intel / Linux | ⚠️ `available()` returns False without the MLX venv; no regression for other streamers | | Windows | ⚠️ No MLX; feature absent, no regression | ## Quick-start guide 1. Set up MLX env + worker per `skills/productivity/local-tts-optimization` (or the companion repo `x7peeps/hermes-tts-kit`) 2. `hermes config set tts.streaming.provider qwen3tts-mlx` 3. Speak to Hermes; voice messages/session speech now stream from the local engine with the cloned voice ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Cause | Fix | |---|---|---| | `available()` False | MLX venv / worker missing | install per the local-tts-optimization skill | | worker exits non-zero | model dir or ref audio path wrong | set `tts.streaming.qwen3tts-mlx.model_dir` / `.ref_audio` | | `check_model_inputs()` error | PYTHONPATH shadowing transformers | ensure `env -u PYTHONPATH` in the subprocess cmd (already in code) | ## Resource guard: local MLX prefetch serialization (2026-08-17) `stream_tts_to_speaker` prefetches the next sentence while the current one plays (Semaphore(3)). For cloud providers that is network-bound and cheap; for the local MLX streamer every concurrent prefetch spawns an extra MLX worker subprocess (2-3GB RAM + GPU each). A 3-way prefetch therefore ran three local inference workers at once — tripling memory pressure and contending for the same GPU. Local streamers are now detected by the `_VENV` attribute they carry and serialize prefetch to 1 slot; cloud streamers keep 3-way. No new config knob; covered by a dedicated regression test (`test_local_mlx_streamer_serializes_prefetch`).

signal.title: fix(desktop): keep active Goals visible in sidebar
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Standing Goals can continue across turns, but the Desktop sidebar status projection did not consume Goal state. When a foreground turn yielded while a Goal remained `active` or `waiting`, its sidebar row could appear idle even though the Goal was still running. This PR adds a stable standing-Goal projection, bridges runtime session IDs through stored-session IDs and lineage aliases, and applies the existing `background` sidebar state without overriding more specific live states (`working`, `stalled`, or `needs-input`). It changes only status presentation; Goal execution is unchanged. ## Related Issue No linked issue. signal.title: feat(desktop): add colorblind-friendly diff colors option
signal.text: ## Summary Adds an opt-in **colorblind mode** for the desktop app. When enabled, file diffs use a blue (add) / orange (remove) pair instead of the default green/red — colors that stay clearly separable under red-green color vision deficiency (deuteranopia / protanopia), where red vs green is exactly the pair that blurs together. ## Motivation Red-green color vision deficiency affects ~8% of men. Diff lines in the desktop app have their leading +/- marker stripped and read by color alone, so the default green/red tint is the least accessible part of the UI for those users. The existing approach required users to inject their own CSS via a desktop plugin; this makes the fix first-class and configurable. ## Changes - **`hermes_cli/config_defaults.py`**: new `desktop.colorblind_mode` key, default `False` (auto-surfaced in the config schema). - **`apps/desktop/src/styles.css`**: `html[data-colorblind='true']` overrides the `--ui-diff-add/remove-*` tokens to the blue/orange pair (light + dark variants), plus the review file-tree status glyphs and +n/−n diff counters inside review rows — scoped so app-wide green/red usage (errors, PR badges) is untouched. - **`apps/desktop/src/app/hooks/use-colorblind-mode.ts`** (new): bridges the config toggle to the `data-colorblind` attribute on `<html>`, mounted in `ContribController` so it applies in every window mode (main + HUD). - **`apps/desktop/src/app/settings/constants.ts`**: `Appearance` section now exposes the field. - **`apps/desktop/src/i18n/zh.ts`**: Chinese label + description (设置 → 配置 → 外观 → 红绿色弱模式). - **`apps/desktop/src/types/hermes.ts`**: typed `colorblind_mode` field. - **`use-colorblind-mode.test.tsx`** (new): 3 tests covering attribute set / unset / toggle-off. ## Behavior - **Default unchanged**: `colorblind_mode` is off by default; the green/red diff palette renders exactly as before unless the user opts in. - Colors in colorblind mode: light `add #0a6cd2 / remove #c2570a`; dark `add #5f9ef8 / remove #ff9e64`; background tint raised to 20–22% for stronger blocks. ## Testing - `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` — clean - `vitest run src/app/hooks/use-colorblind-mode.test.tsx` — 3/3 passed - Schema probe: `desktop.colorblind_mode` present in `_build_schema_from_config(DEFAULT_CONFIG)` (type boolean) - Local build (`npm run build` + electron-builder) verified; toggle verified in the built app
